# Product

## Register

product

## Users

Writers, editors, researchers, and technically comfortable creators who want a focused drafting room with structured editorial feedback. They are usually trying to move from a vague brief or partial draft into a clearer manuscript, then export or publish it.

## Product Purpose

Twyne is a local-first writing desk with an AI-assisted room of editors. It helps writers define a project dossier, draft in rich text, receive persona feedback, score work against a rubric, manage citations, sync across devices when signed in, and publish or export finished work. Success means the writer keeps ownership and momentum while the product makes revision concrete.

## Brand Personality

Editorial, exacting, literary. The product should feel like a working writer's room rather than generic SaaS: opinionated, calm, and serious about craft without getting precious.

## Anti-references

Do not make Twyne look like a generic AI chat app, a growth dashboard, a blank note-taking clone, or a loud marketing funnel. Avoid decorative UI that competes with the manuscript, vague AI productivity claims, and controls that obscure where drafts and keys are stored.

## Design Principles

- Keep the manuscript central.
- Make data movement explicit: local, synced, published, or sent to a provider.
- Use standard controls for standard tasks, dressed in Twyne's editorial system.
- Prefer concise copy that names the actual action.
- Preserve writer trust through clear export, privacy, and account controls.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Aim for WCAG AA contrast and keyboard-operable controls. Important interactions should work with semantic HTML where possible. Respect reduced-motion preferences, avoid color-only state, and keep long-form reading comfortable on mobile and desktop.

content.text:
I haven't changed any code. This is the review you asked for, based on reading the routes and editor components. I didn't run the app, so I haven't seen how any of it looks in a browser.

## 1. Styling inconsistencies across pages

**Page shells fall into three families.** The same kind of page is built three different ways:
- **Soft paper group:** `analysis`, `apparatus`, `library`, `personas`, `rubric`, `settings`, `account` and `signin` use `bg-[var(--color-paper-soft)]` with `min-h-screen`.
- **Plain paper group:** `desk`, `privacy-ledger` and `onboarding` use `--color-paper` instead.
- **No full-height shell:** `pricing` uses a bare `<main>`.

**Content widths are all different.** There is no shared measure:

| Page | Width |
|---|---|
| `analysis`, `library`, `rubric`, `apparatus`, `signin` | 5xl |
| `personas`, `account`, `privacy-ledger` | 4xl |
| `settings` | 4xl, with 2xl inner blocks |
| `desk` | 6xl |
| `legal-page` (privacy, terms, faq, downloads) | 3xl |
| `pricing` | 5xl, with inner 3xl, 2xl and prose |
| `[handle]` | 2xl |

Horizontal padding also varies between `px-6`, `px-4 sm:px-8` and `px-5 sm:px-8`.

**Page headings are copy-pasted rather than shared.**
- `analysis`, `account`, `apparatus`, `library`, `personas`, `rubric` and `settings` each repeat an inline-style `<h1>` with 1.75rem, weight 700 and `--font-display`.
- `pricing` uses `text-3xl sm:text-4xl` in `--font-serif`.
- `signin` uses `text-4xl sm:text-5xl`.
- `onboarding` uses 1.8rem and 1.6rem in two different steps.
- `privacy-ledger` uses `font-display text-3xl`.
- `docs` uses a bare `<h1>`.
- Only the first group has the `dept-label` eyebrow above the title.

**Styling is written three ways.** Some pages use Tailwind classes, some use inline `style={{…}}` objects for fonts, and some use scoped CSS. `onboarding` has 24 inline `font-family` declarations, `downloads` 13, `[handle]` 15 and `apparatus` 12. Other pages set the font once at the shell level.

**Border radius is inconsistent.** The editorial system looks square-cornered (2–4px), but `settings` has 10 `rounded-full` and 2 `rounded-lg`, and `pricing` has `rounded-md` and `rounded-full`. `onboarding`, `dossier/create` and `settings` use `rounded-[3px]`. Elsewhere, 2px, 3px, 4px and 999px all appear.

**Buttons aren't used uniformly.** `btn-paper` and `btn-press` are the house buttons. `downloads`, `faq` and `[handle]` use neither, and `signin` and `onboarding` use `btn-press` only. `settings` mixes both.

**Loading states differ per page.**
- The editor says "Press Room / Setting the type…".
- `onboarding` says "Loading the room…".
- `analysis` has a plain "Loading…".
- `desk` has "Reading the ledger".
- `EditorialLoader` exists but is only used inside `analysis`, `rubric-panel` and `personas-panel`.

**Suggested fix:** add one `<PageShell width="…">` with a `<PageHeader eyebrow title lede>`, built on the `legal-page` pattern. Use three width tokens (reading 3xl, standard 5xl, wide 6xl). Move the heading style into `global.css`.

## 2. Using space better in the editor

- **The text column is narrow by default.** `DEFAULT_LAYOUT` has `width: "normal"` (48rem, about 768px), and 2rem side margins cut that to about 640px of text. Wide mode is 62rem. The canvas is centered with `mx-auto`, so a 1440px window with both sidebars closed still shows a lot of dead paper.
- **The drawer is 18rem (`w-72`), and the right panel defaults to 340px.** With both open on a laptop, the writer gets very little. Another reply in this review path (the `onWindowResize` handler) only undocks them on phones.
- **`PageRuler`, the compositor toolbar and the sticky tools stack are all above the text.** On a short laptop screen that's a lot of vertical chrome before the first line.
- **Suggestions:**
  - Make the default width fluid, for example `min(100% - gutters, 56rem)`, or give the continuous mode a character measure (`~68ch`) instead of a fixed rem.
  - Auto-collapse the drawer while typing and reopen it on hover or Escape.
  - Fold the ruler into the page-setup panel, hidden unless wanted.
  - Make the right panel an overlay below about 1280px, as the Editorial Board already is.
  - Keep margin notes in the gutter beside the page, so they use the unused paper rather than adding a panel.

## 3. Why the editor has to load, and what to do about it

There are **two sequential waits**, and neither shows the page.

1. **Local data read** (`routes/editor/index.tsx`, `useVisibleTask$` around line 262). It runs after the client mounts. It reads folios, the folio's content, the dossier, editions and migrations from IndexedDB, then sets `store.hydrated = true`. Until then the whole route, including the drawer, masthead and toolbar, is replaced by the "Press Room / Setting the type…" card (line 1110). The data is local-first, so there is nothing to wait on from a server. The wait is the sequential `await`s, with Qwik's client-only task start on top.
2. **TipTap mount** (`twyne-editor.tsx`, line 927). Only after step 1 does the editor component mount, `import("@tiptap/core")` and `loadPersonasFromIdb`, and then it builds the editor into `#twyne-editor-mount`. That div is empty in the meantime, so the page appears blank before the text pops in.

**Why it exists:** IndexedDB, and the check that decides whether to redirect to `/dossier/create/`, only work in the browser. TipTap needs the DOM.

**Better options, in order of payoff:**
1. **Remove the full-screen gate.** Render the real shell (drawer, masthead, page canvas) immediately. Only the manuscript body waits.
2. **Show the content first.** Paint the folio's saved HTML as a static, non-editable preview in the canvas as soon as the IndexedDB read finishes, then swap in TipTap. Writers see their words at once, and the swap is invisible if the typography matches.
3. **Run the reads in parallel.** `Promise.all` the folio content, dossier, editions and personas, and prefetch `@tiptap/core` while IndexedDB reads.
4. **If a placeholder is still needed**, use a few skeleton text lines in the page canvas, not a spinner card. A 150ms delay before showing anything avoids a flash on fast loads. Respect reduced motion.
5. **Cache the last folio's HTML** in a small `localStorage` key so the first paint doesn't wait for IndexedDB.

Doing 1–2 would probably remove the loading screen for most people.

Want me to start with the editor loading changes (items 1–3), or the shared `PageShell` and `PageHeader` first?

Going further if we were to codify this practice of adding juice to the user interface, look at each of the interfaces in the desk and writers room each of the components. Think about how we could add shaders and animations and variants that help communicate what this interaction does and why you should or should not interact with it. You can do your research on similar things online but also consider gaps that mighth be missing thata fit right in here. Continue until you have come up with a way for each component to 'give joy' making the user experience smooth but also different from other more generic editors. The editor should have an identity it is trying to communicate whether thaht is is as you move you mouse around, type something, scroll or drag. We should consider important interactions that seem well suited but also enjoyable. There should be a sense that this application is living. You will need to demonstrate properly how you managed to do this and what choices you made and why as well as compare those surfaces afterwards.

I'll take inventory of every surface on the desk and in the editor, then capture "before" screenshots, define a motion vocabulary, build it, and compare before and after. First I'm reading the existing motion code, the product principles and my browser-verification notes.

This project uses [Convex](https://convex.dev) as its backend.

When working on Convex code, **always read `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` first** for important guidelines on how to correctly use Convex APIs and patterns. The file contains rules that override what you may have learned about Convex from training data.

=====
# Product

## Register

product

## Users

Writers, editors, researchers, and technically comfortable creators who want a focused drafting room with structured editorial feedback. They are usually trying to move from a vague brief or partial draft into a clearer manuscript, then export or publish it.

## Product Purpose

Twyne is a local-first writing desk with an AI-assisted room of editors. It helps writers define a project dossier, draft in rich text, receive persona feedback, score work against a rubric, manage citations, sync across devices when signed in, and publish or export finished work. Success means the writer keeps ownership and momentum while the product makes revision concrete.

## Brand Personality

Editorial, exacting, literary. The product should feel like a working writer's room rather than generic SaaS: opinionated, calm, and serious about craft without getting precious.

## Anti-references

Do not make Twyne look like a generic AI chat app, a growth dashboard, a blank note-taking clone, or a loud marketing funnel. Avoid decorative UI that competes with the manuscript, vague AI productivity claims, and controls that obscure where drafts and keys are stored.

## Design Principles

- Keep the manuscript central.
- Make data movement explicit: local, synced, published, or sent to a provider.
- Use standard controls for standard tasks, dressed in Twyne's editorial system.
- Prefer concise copy that names the actual action.
- Preserve writer trust through clear export, privacy, and account controls.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Aim for WCAG AA contrast and keyboard-operable controls. Important interactions should work with semantic HTML where possible. Respect reduced-motion preferences, avoid color-only state, and keep long-form reading comfortable on mobile and desktop.

input.description: Research editor UI juice and motion
input.prompt:
Research task (web), no code changes. I'm designing an interaction-motion identity for Twyne, a literary writing app (local-first rich-text editor + an AI "room of editors" that leave margin notes, a rubric that "stamps" a draft, a stats "Desk" page). Brand: editorial letterpress — paper, ink, type, stamps, vermilion and cobalt, a writers' room. I want motion, shaders and component variants that (a) communicate what an interaction does and whether you should/shouldn't do it (consequence: local vs synced vs sent to an AI provider vs published vs destructive), (b) make the app feel alive, (c) never harm writing performance or legibility, (d) are distinctive versus generic editors (Notion, Google Docs, Word).

Please find and summarise, with source URLs:
1. "Game feel"/"juice" principles applied to productivity UI (e.g. Jonasson & Purho "Juice it or lose it", Rauno Freiberg "Invisible details of interaction design", Emil Kowalski on animation craft, Linear/Raycast/Arc/Things motion writing, Apple HIG motion). Extract concrete, reusable rules (durations, easing, when not to animate, frequency of interaction vs animation budget).
2. Editors with distinctive typing/caret/scroll feel: Microsoft Word smooth caret/typing animation, VS Code smooth caret, iA Writer focus/typewriter mode, Ulysses, Bear, Craft, Obsidian, Monkeytype caret, Typora, Hemingway, Paper by WeTransfer/FiftyThree, Teenage Engineering-style UIs. What exactly do they animate and how is it received (any complaints about distraction/latency)?
3. Ink, paper and letterpress effects on the web: ink-bleed / wet-ink shaders, paper grain/fibre normal maps lit by a moving light, letterpress debossing via CSS, risograph/halftone shaders, stamp impressions. Prefer techniques that are cheap (WebGL fragment shaders at reduced resolution, CSS only, SVG filters) and note performance pitfalls (SVG filters on large areas, backdrop-filter).
4. Modern browser APIs useful here, with current support status (2025-2026): CSS Custom Highlight API (`::highlight()` — which properties are allowed, can it animate?), View Transitions API (same-document), scroll-driven animations (`animation-timeline: scroll()/view()`), `@property` registered custom properties for animating gradients, `linear()` easing for springs, Popover API + `@starting-style`, `interpolate-size`, WebGPU vs WebGL2 availability.
5. Patterns that communicate consequence/trust in UI motion: hold-to-confirm for destructive actions, "sending" vs "saving" animations, rate-limit/out-of-credits states, disabled-with-reason affordances, AI "thinking" indicators that aren't generic spinners (e.g. shimmer text, reading-progress indicators). Note which are considered good vs gimmicky.
6. Anything about "ambient life" in UI: presence indicators (Figma cursors), breathing idle states, time-of-day lighting, and accessibility guidance (prefers-reduced-motion, vestibular triggers, WCAG 2.3.3, avoiding parallax for long reading).

Deliver a compact report (under ~1500 words): bullet points grouped by the six headings, each bullet with a concrete takeaway and a URL. Flag anything you could not verify. Finish with a list of 10 "gaps": ideas that fit a literary editor + AI editors and are rarely done well elsewhere.

Research task (web), no code changes. "Game feel"/"juice" principles applied to productivity UI (e.g. Jonasson & Purho "Juice it or lose it", Rauno Freiberg "Invisible details of interaction design", Emil Kowalski on animation craft, Linear/Raycast/Arc/Things motion writing, Apple HIG motion). description: "Don't block on the full test suite or repeated typecheck runs in twyne; targeted checks only, then hand back"
metadata:

In twyne, don't run the full `bun run test` suite (it takes over 10 minutes) or keep re-running `tsc` after every edit. When the work is done, stop and report back.

**Why:** On 2026-10-11 the user stopped a persona/voice redesign while it waited on the full suite and said "stop with the typechecking, move on without the tests."

**How to apply:** Run only the targeted test files for the code you changed, at most once, and only if they're quick. Never wait in a loop for long suites. In the summary, say which checks you skipped.
name: autonomy-by-default
description: "Twyne should act on its own by default — reviews, research, editor readings run without the writer clicking; buttons are optional overrides"
metadata:
  type: feedback

Twyne's default is autonomous, fluid action: editors read, research runs, reviews complete, and results arrive without the writer having to press a button. Manual controls may exist as options (re-run, steer, decline), but a feature that waits for a click before doing its core job is a design defect.

**Why:** The user (Keith Noel's product direction, restated by the owner 2026-10-20) said "waiting for the user to click a button is not what I want for this app… the default is autonomous fluid action."

**How to apply:** When building or fixing a feature, ask "does this happen if the writer never clicks?" If not, add an automatic trigger (on draft change / idle / panel open / folio open) with spend guards (dedupe per draft fingerprint, rate floors, session caps) rather than a call-to-action button. Empty states should say what the app is about to do on its own, not invite a click. Hosted (non-BYOK) users must get the autonomous path too. Related: [[skip-long-verification]].
name: no-reflexive-hedging
description: "Don't attach trust/uncertainty caveats to every claim in designs or product copy (e.g. \"sources aren't trustworthy\" on research cards)"

**How to apply:** Mention a limitation only when it changes the design or a decision. Related: [[autonomy-by-default]].

# eslint-plugin-qwik-guards

Shared ESLint guardrails for Qwik projects. The rules cover an empty-list
reconciliation path and plain-function JSX form wrappers, both of which have
caused fields to be replaced and lose focus in Twyne.

The empty-array runtime failure was reproduced on **Qwik 2.0.0-rc.4**. The form
wrapper rule covers a historical **Qwik 2 beta.42** failure, checked against the
actual source before and after its fix; that older runtime was not rerun during
plugin verification. Enable this preset deliberately in affected projects. It
does not detect your installed Qwik version or establish behavior on other
versions. It complements
`eslint-plugin-qwik` and does not replace it.

## Install in another project

Registry installation:

```sh
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-qwik-guards
```

The package is build-free ESM, has no runtime dependencies, and expects ESLint 9 and
Node 20.19 or newer. TypeScript projects keep their existing TypeScript ESLint
parser configuration.

To share a checkout or prerelease without a registry, produce a portable archive
from this package directory:

```sh
npm pack --pack-destination /tmp
```

In the target project:

```sh
npm install --save-dev /tmp/eslint-plugin-qwik-guards-0.1.0.tgz
```

Add the preset to the project's existing flat ESLint config, after its parser
configuration. Restrict `files` to the project's Qwik source roots if it contains
other frameworks:

```js
import qwikGuards from "eslint-plugin-qwik-guards";

export default [
  // Existing ESLint, Qwik, and TypeScript configurations go here.
  {
    ...qwikGuards.configs.recommended,
    files: ["src/**/*.{jsx,tsx}"],
  },
];
```

The preset enables `qwik-guards/no-empty-array-before-sibling` and
`qwik-guards/no-plain-jsx-form-wrapper` at `warn` severity.
To block merges after existing sites have been reviewed, override the rules to
`error` in a later config entry, or use ESLint's `--max-warnings 0` policy.

input.content:
# The living press

Twyne's interface is a working press room, not a document viewer. Most editors animate to seem modern. Here, motion has three jobs:

1. **Answer.** When a writer presses something, the room shows that it took the press.
2. **Say where things go.** Every action that sends words somewhere looks like it is sending them there, in the same ink every time.
3. **Show that the room is alive.** Editors read, ink dries and the light moves. None of it gets in the way of writing.

This page is the contract for all of it. The tokens live in [`src/styles/motion.css`](../../src/styles/motion.css), the levels and typing signal in [`src/utils/motion.ts`](../../src/utils/motion.ts), and the destinations in [`src/utils/consequence.ts`](../../src/utils/consequence.ts).

## Five rules

1. **The manuscript never moves.** Nothing translates, scales or reflows prose, and nothing lays out again because something animated. Ink may change colour on the page. Popovers, slips and margins move around the page, never on it.
2. **Frequency sets the budget.** The more often something happens, the less it may move.

   | How often | Example | Allowed |
   |---|---|---|
   | Every keystroke | typing, caret | colour only, at most one DOM write per burst, no transform |
   | Many times a minute | hover, a press | ≤ `--dur-press` / `--dur-release` (120 / 160 ms), 1px of travel |
   | A few times a minute | menus, popovers, a note arriving | ≤ `--dur-arrive` / `--dur-settle` (240 / 320 ms) |
   | A few times a session | a verdict, a publish, a first save | ≤ `--dur-ceremony` (900 ms), may use a shader |
   | Ambient | the desk lamp, an editor reading | slower than one cycle per 5 s, paused while typing |

   Keyboard-initiated actions skip their entrance where the result appears under the hands, as in command palettes and shortcuts.
3. **Consequence has one ink.** A control that sends something somewhere carries `data-consequence` and, wherever space allows, a [`<DestinationTag>`](../../src/components/ui/destination-tag.tsx). The ink is never the only cue. Every destination also has a word and a mark shape.
4. **Ambient life rests.** Anything nobody asked for carries `data-ambient` (or `.is-ambient`). It pauses while `html[data-typing]` is set, during flow and settling, and below the `full` level. Ambient work must not run per frame: it renders when its inputs change, not on a loop.
5. **Still is still.** `html[data-motion="still"]` collapses every duration. Colour and opacity changes remain, because WCAG 2.3.3 counts movement, not colour. So every state needs a colour or wording cue that does not depend on travel.

## Levels

The writer picks the level in **Preferences → Appearance → Motion**. It is stored on the device and stamped onto `<html data-motion>` before first paint.

| Level | Feedback & arrivals | Ceremonies | Ambient |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | yes | full length | yes, resting while typing |
| `calm` | yes | shortened (`--dur-ceremony` 360 ms) | no |
| `still` | no movement; colour only | no movement | no |

`system` (the default) resolves to `full`, or to `still` when the operating system asks for reduced motion. In script, use `allowsMotion("feedback" | "ceremony" | "ambient")` instead of reading `matchMedia` directly. Shaders must check it before allocating a context.

## Tokens

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--ease-set` | `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)` | the house curve; most transitions |
| `--ease-lift` | `cubic-bezier(.55,0,1,.45)` | things leaving |
| `--ease-slip` | spring `linear()`, ~3% overshoot | paper in hand: slips, notes, popovers |
| `--ease-platen` | spring `linear()`, <1% overshoot | stamps, presses, anything heavy |
| `--dur-press` / `--dur-release` | 120 / 160 ms | presses, hovers |
| `--dur-arrive` / `--dur-settle` | 240 / 320 ms | menus, slips / panels, cards |
| `--dur-ceremony` | 900 ms | verdicts, publishing |
| `--dur-dry` | 1600 ms | fresh ink drying after a save |
| `--dur-breath` | 9 s | ambient cycles |
| `--lift-1/2/3` | 1px / .25rem / .6rem | travel distances |

Shared keyframes: `press-slip-in`, `press-slip-in-from-right`, `press-fade-in`, `press-ink-flash` (tint with `--flash-ink`), and `press-impress`. Utility classes: `.press-arrive`, `.press-arrive-right`, `.press-fade`.

## Consequence grammar

| `data-consequence` | Ink | Mark | Word | Means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `local` | ink-muted | hollow ring | device | stays on this device |
| `synced` | green | filled dot | account | copied to the writer's own account |
| `provider` | cobalt | filled dot | model | read by the writer's own model provider (BYOK) |
| `credit` | mustard | filled dot | credit | read by a hosted model; spends credit |
| `public` | vermilion | ring with dot | public | readable by anyone with the link, or a PDS |
| `erase` | deep vermilion | struck square | erases | removed and cannot be brought back here |

`aiConsequenceFor(settings)` / `loadAiConsequence()` decide between `provider` and `credit` from the writer's saved settings, so a tag tells the truth about the route a request will take.

**Guards scale with the loss.**

- Anything recoverable gets no confirmation. Undo is enough.
- A loss that is recoverable elsewhere (restore keeps a checkpoint) gets an inline confirm.
- A loss that cannot be recovered from here (erase synced history, stop sharing, unpublish) gets [`<HoldToConfirm>`](../../src/components/ui/hold-to-confirm.tsx). The platen comes down while the control is held, and releasing early drains the ink. Keyboard and assistive technology use a two-step press instead.

## The joy ledger

Each surface gets one idea that belongs to a press room and nowhere else. The table lists what it is, what it says, and why it suits that surface.

### The manuscript (lane A)

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| Typing | **Wet ink.** New words are set in a slightly bluer, wetter ink until they are stored on the device, then dry to black over `--dur-dry`. Uses the CSS Custom Highlight API, so no DOM, layout or transform is touched. | Your words are safe the moment they dry. If ink stays wet, the save hasn't landed. |
| Caret | A vermilion caret, the editor's pencil. Never smoothed or animated, because Word's gliding caret is the cautionary tale. | Where the hand is. Instant. |
| Selection | Non-photo blue, the copy editor's proof pencil, instead of the system highlight. | A marked passage, ready for a decision. |
| Selection popover | Slides up off the line like a slip pushed across the desk. Every AI action carries its destination tag. | Which actions stay here and which send the passage to a model, before you press. |
| Section drag | The ⋮⋮ handle becomes a type slug that lifts on grab, and the drop is a vermilion composing rule. | Moving a section is moving set type: the whole block goes. |
| File drop | "Drop a plate" with the destination written on the docket: kept in the manuscript on this device, or uploaded to your account's storage. | Where the image will live before you let go. |
| The desk lamp | A soft light pools on the paper's grain behind the page. It drifts with the hour and leans toward the pointer only when you are not typing. | The room is lit and inhabited, and quiet while you write. |

### The editor chrome (lane B)

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| Drawer | Folios slide out like a drawer of filed sheets. The active folio wears a tab, and switching moves the tab. | Which manuscript is on the desk. |
| Masthead | The wordmark's ink sits still while you type. The infinite wobble now plays only at rest, as ambient life. | A press at rest and a press at work. |
| Save and sync | One status line instead of two dots. It reads *set* on save, *on the wire* while syncing, and *filed* when the account has it. | Exactly where the latest words are. |
| Menus and popovers | One arrival everywhere: `--dur-arrive` with `--ease-slip` from the trigger side. One scrim value. | Menus belong to what opened them. |
| Publish and share | Publish is a ceremony: the button inks in vermilion as the page goes out. Unpublish and stop-sharing are held, not clicked. | Public actions look public, and permanent ones resist a slip. |
| Zen and flow | Chrome eases out as one sheet, not piece by piece, and returns the same way. | The room steps back as a whole when you write. |

### The writers' room (lane C)

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| An editor reading | The portrait of an editor who is reading wears a slow pencil-mark ring, its progress tied to the real stream (reasoning → writing → filed). There is no spinner. | Who is reading your draft right now, and how far they have got. |
| A note arriving | The note is set like a slip pushed onto the board. On filing it takes a small ink impression in the editor's colour. | Something new is on the board, and from whom. |
| Asking the room | Each AI button carries its destination tag (model or credit). | Before pressing: whose model reads this, and whether it costs. |
| The rubric verdict | The grade stamp presses with an ink-impression shader: a halftone corona with mis-registered vermilion and cobalt. Ceremony class, played once per new verdict. | The judgement is in, and it is weighty. |
| Marginalia | Strike draws a line through the card. Erase is held. | Settled versus gone. |
| Apparatus | Sources being searched carry a reading tick in cobalt. When found they file with a mustard flash. | Research is happening and something was found. |

### My Desk (lane D)

| Surface | The idea | What it communicates |
|---|---|---|
| Opening the ledger | Figures are set like a composing stick: numerals roll into place once on arrival and never again while the page is open. | A dossier being prepared for you. |
| Range | Switching range keeps the old figures in place and re-sets only what changed. No flash of the loader. | The same desk, a different window of time. |
| Heatmap | Selecting a day presses its cell, and the selected-day aside slides in like a ledger page. | Which day you are reading. |
| Charts | Bars rise from the baseline once, on arrival. | Activity accumulating, not decoration. |
| Patterns | When a pattern unlocks it gets a small *filed* stamp. | Evidence has accumulated. |
| Hosted charges | Money figures use the credit ink, and refreshing re-sets only the changed numerals. | This is the part that costs. |

## Performance contract

- Nothing new runs per keystroke beyond `markTyping()` (a timer reset) and, for wet ink, one range append per transaction.
- The derived save path (`twyne:draft-saved`) drives drying, so drying costs nothing while the writer is typing.
- Shaders render on a small canvas, at most 256 CSS px on a side and at half resolution. They run for a ceremony and then free the context. They never run behind the manuscript on a loop.
- The desk lamp is a CSS gradient on a registered property. It is set on pointer idle and once a minute for the hour, never per frame.
- `bun run test:typing` is the arbiter. A change that moves its numbers is a regression, whatever it looks like.

## Adding to it

New motion names a row in the joy ledger. It says what it communicates, uses only the tokens above, has a `still` state that keeps the meaning, and carries `data-ambient` if nobody asked for it. If it sends anything anywhere, it carries a consequence.

input.title: Living press · Lane B · editor chrome
input.task:
You are Lane B of a four-lane effort called "the living press" in Twyne, a Qwik 2 + TipTap local-first writing app (editorial letterpress brand: paper, ink, stamps, vermilion and cobalt). Your worktree starts from commit 0fd76e12 on branch feat/living-press, which contains the shared foundation. Commit your work on your own branch; the parent merges it.

## Read first (the contract)
- docs/design/living-press.md: the five rules, the frequency budget, the consequence grammar, and your rows in "The joy ledger → The editor chrome (lane B)". Implement those rows.
- src/styles/motion.css: tokens (--ease-set, --ease-lift, --ease-slip, --ease-platen, --dur-press/release/arrive/settle/ceremony/dry/breath, --lift-1/2/3), consequence inks (--ink-local/synced/provider/credit/public/erase via [data-consequence] → var(--consequence-ink)), shared keyframes press-slip-in, press-slip-in-from-right, press-fade-in, press-ink-flash, press-impress, and classes .press-arrive/.press-arrive-right/.press-fade. Ambient motion must carry data-ambient (paused automatically while html[data-typing], in flow/settling, and below full). html[data-motion="still"] collapses durations globally.
- src/utils/motion.ts (allowsMotion, motionLevel, onMotionLevelChange, markTyping/isTyping), src/utils/consequence.ts (Consequence type, aiConsequenceFor, loadAiConsequence), src/components/ui/destination-tag.tsx (<DestinationTag to="public" />), src/components/ui/hold-to-confirm.tsx (<HoldToConfirm onConfirm$ label hint consequence="erase">…</HoldToConfirm>).

## Files you own (edit ONLY these, plus new files you create under src/components/editor/chrome/ if needed)
- src/styles/press-chrome.css (your stylesheet; already imported from global.css: put ALL your new CSS here, do not edit global.css)
- src/routes/editor/index.tsx (drawer, masthead, sign-in toast, hydration gate, board toggle, zen/flow handling)
- src/components/folio/folio-menu.tsx (File menu, import modal, share/publish modal)
- src/components/collaboration/share-dialog.tsx
- src/components/auth/account-menu.tsx
- src/components/editor/sync-indicator.tsx and sync-indicator-helpers.ts
- src/components/editor/typst-workspace.tsx (+ typst-workspace.css)
- src/components/editor/compositor-panel.tsx (only open/close of pickers/popovers and tab indicator; do not restructure)
- src/components/editor/shortcut-dialog.tsx
- src/components/brief/project-brief-card.tsx
Do NOT edit: src/global.css, src/styles/motion.css, other press-*.css files, src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx, manuscript-panel.tsx, selection-actions.tsx, anything under personas/rubric/comments/citations/editorial-board/living-desk/instruments/desk. Other lanes own those, and your branch must merge cleanly.

## What to build (concrete)
1. Drawer: slides like a drawer of filed sheets. The active folio wears a vermilion tab (a small ::before mark) that moves to the newly active row on switch (use a transition on a shared indicator, or animate the new row's tab in with --ease-slip; keep it cheap). Inner content fades/slides with the width change instead of being clipped. The drawer toggle icon reflects open/closed (aria-expanded + a visual state).
2. Masthead: the TWYNE wordmark's `.press` infinite wobble must become ambient: give the wordmark data-ambient so it rests while typing/in flow/below full. Do not edit global.css's .press rule; add the attribute in index.tsx.
3. Save and sync status line: replace the bare SyncDot + "Saved Xs ago" pairing in the status bar with one status line whose words say where the latest words are: "set" (stored on this device), "on the wire" (syncing), "filed" (in the account), "held on this device" (offline/local-only/error with reason). Use the consequence inks (local hollow, synced green). Animate only state changes (a brief press-ink-flash with --flash-ink on transition to filed), never a perpetual pulse. Remove the duplicate SyncDot in the compositor quick actions if it is the same indicator (sync-indicator.tsx is yours; compositor-panel.tsx usage line is yours to change).
4. Menus and popovers: give the File menu dropdown, AccountMenu dropdown, ShareDialog popover, compositor pickers, the Typst status popover and the shortcut dialog ONE consistent arrival: --dur-arrive with --ease-slip, translating --lift-2 from the trigger side, plus press-fade-in for scrims. Use one scrim colour token for all modal scrims (define it in press-chrome.css, e.g. --scrim: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-ink) 55%, transparent)). Prefer CSS-only (@starting-style or keyframes on mount). Nothing may delay interactivity.
5. Publish and share (folio-menu.tsx and share-dialog.tsx): add <DestinationTag> to: Publish now (public), PDS publish (public), Micropub (public), Invite (synced, or public if it shares beyond the account; read the code), Share this folio (synced), exports (local). Publish success becomes a short ceremony: the button inks vermilion across (use --press-progress or a keyframe with --dur-ceremony and --ease-platen) and settles to a "published" state. Unpublish, Unpublish from PDS, remove collaborator and Stop sharing use <HoldToConfirm consequence="erase"> (or "public" for unpublish if you judge the loss as un-publishing; state your reasoning in the report). Stop sharing currently opens a ThemedDialog; replacing the dialog with a hold is fine if focus/keyboard behaviour is preserved.
6. Hydration gate ("Press Room / Setting the type…" around index.tsx line 1110): keep it but make it calm and on-brand: a press-fade with a 150ms delay so fast loads never flash it, and a quiet set-type line (e.g. a row of slugs filling) marked data-ambient. Do NOT restructure hydration; a separate effort will remove the gate.
7. Sign-in toast: arrive with press-slip-in from below, use the shared --shade-based shadow instead of the hard-coded rgba, radius 2px like the rest.
8. Zen and flow: when zen toggles, chrome eases out/in as one sheet: a single opacity+translate transition on the masthead and compositor using --dur-settle and --ease-set. Fix the dead `.zen-masthead` hover strip: either make it work (a thin hover strip that reveals the masthead) or remove the class usage from index.tsx; explain the choice.
9. Disabled states: undo/redo in compositor use opacity .4 like .btn-press (they use .3 today); .typst-apply needs a visible disabled style (typst-workspace.css).

## Rules
- The manuscript never moves. Nothing you add may shift prose layout.
- Durations and easing come only from the tokens. No new hard-coded cubic-beziers, no transition: all.
- Every state you animate also has a colour or wording cue (for still mode).
- Keep accessibility: aria-expanded/aria-pressed correct, focus returned on close, keyboard paths intact, HoldToConfirm keyboard flow works.
- Match the surrounding code's comment density and idiom (Qwik component$, useSignal, class arrays). Don't add stock caveat copy.
- Performance: no per-frame JS, no listeners on keystrokes.

## Verify before you finish
- `bun install` if node_modules is missing; `bun run prompts:compile && bun run i18n:prepare` once.
- `npx eslint <your changed files>` clean (warnings only if pre-existing).

input.title: Living press · Lane C · writers' room

Brand: editorial letterpress (paper, ink, stamps, vermilion and cobalt). Your worktree starts from commit 0fd76e12 on branch feat/living-press, which contains the shared foundation. Commit your work on your own branch; the parent merges it.

## Read first (the contract)
- docs/design/living-press.md: the five rules, the frequency budget, the consequence grammar, and your rows in "The joy ledger → The writers' room (lane C)". Implement those rows.
- src/styles/motion.css: tokens (--ease-set, --ease-lift, --ease-slip, --ease-platen, --dur-press/release/arrive/settle/ceremony/dry/breath, --lift-1/2/3), consequence inks via [data-consequence] → var(--consequence-ink) (--ink-provider cobalt, --ink-credit mustard, --ink-synced green, --ink-erase deep vermilion), shared keyframes press-slip-in, press-slip-in-from-right, press-fade-in, press-ink-flash (tint via --flash-ink), press-impress, classes .press-arrive/.press-arrive-right/.press-fade. Ambient motion must carry data-ambient (auto-paused while html[data-typing], in flow/settling, and below full). html[data-motion="still"] collapses durations globally.
- src/utils/motion.ts (allowsMotion("feedback"|"ceremony"|"ambient"), motionLevel, onMotionLevelChange), src/utils/consequence.ts (aiConsequenceFor(settings) → "provider" | "credit"; loadAiConsequence()), src/components/ui/destination-tag.tsx (<DestinationTag to={consequence} />), src/components/ui/hold-to-confirm.tsx.

## Files you own (edit ONLY these, plus new files under src/components/rubric/, src/components/personas/, src/components/ui/ that you create)

Other lanes own those.

## What to build (concrete)
1. An editor reading (personas-panel.tsx). Today the only cue is an `animate-spin ✦` on the button plus a text stamp "thinking…/writing…". Replace the spinner with a reading state on the persona's own portrait/face in the cast row and on the streaming card's masthead: a slow pencil-mark ring (SVG circle with stroke-dasharray / conic-gradient on a registered property) whose progress follows the real stream: reasoning phase → ring traced partway, text phase → ring advancing with received characters (cap it), filed → ring closes and fades. Use `GenerationStreamSnapshot` (src/utils/generation-stream.ts: activePart reasoning|text, status, textStatus, reasoningStatus) and the store fields streamingNotes / isGenerating / backgroundRoom.status. No spinner, no shimmer text. When the background room is reading (backgroundRoom.status === "reading"), the cast faces show a faint shared reading mark (ambient: data-ambient). Keep the "thinking…/writing…" stamp words: they are the still-mode cue.
2. A note arriving. The filed note card (feedback-enter, feedbackSlide 0.35s in scoped CSS) should arrive as a slip pushed onto the board: press-slip-in with --ease-slip, staggered ≤50ms when several land together (cap the stagger at 6). On filing (streaming card → filed card swap), the masthead gets a small ink impression in the editor's colour (press-ink-flash with --flash-ink set to the persona colour) once. The thread reply already has persona-reply-enter/caret; wire the unused `.is-fresh` / persona-reply-settle glow so a newly finished reply settles once.
3. Asking the room. Add <DestinationTag> (computed with loadAiConsequence() or aiConsequenceFor(store.aiSettings) where settings are loaded) to: Get notes, Propose edits, Full analysis, reply send, Ask for a fix, Ask them now / Grade again / Grade this draft (rubric), Send to editor (comments-panel), steering composer in editorial-board-overlay, Apparatus retry. One tag per action group is fine where several buttons sit together; don't clutter. The `.provider-pill` already shows the provider after a run; keep it.
4. The rubric verdict. Bring StampShader back (src/components/rubric/stamp-shader.tsx, a WebGL corona; currently imported nowhere; it was removed from grade-stamp.tsx in commit 0cb77885: `git show 0cb77885 -- src/components/rubric/grade-stamp.tsx` to see how it was wired). Rework it into an ink-impression shader that fits the brand: a short (≤ --dur-ceremony, ~900ms) halftone/ink-spread impression with slight mis-registration of vermilion and cobalt plates, behind/around the grade stamp, played only when a NEW verdict lands (resultFresh / impressionKey changes), never on restore. Requirements: check allowsMotion("ceremony") before creating the WebGL context; canvas ≤ 256 CSS px and render at half device-pixel-ratio; stop and lose the context (WEBGL_lose_context) when done; no loop afterwards; honour theme (read --color-vermilion/--color-cobalt from computed style). Calm level: shorten (use the --dur-ceremony computed value). Still: no shader at all. Also make the existing stamp-die-press keyframes use the platen feel where you can do so in press-room.css without editing global.css (e.g. override animation-timing-function on the relevant class with --ease-platen).
5. Marginalia (comments-panel.tsx): striking a comment draws a line through the card (a scaleX rule with --dur-settle), not just opacity. Erase ✕ (permanent, no confirmation today) becomes <HoldToConfirm consequence="erase" label="Erase this comment" hint="hold to erase">. Strike the room (personas clearRoom, also no confirmation) → HoldToConfirm as well.
6. Apparatus (citations-panel.tsx): the deep-trace items that are "searching" get a cobalt reading tick (replace the inline `pulse 1.4s`, mark it data-ambient); when an item becomes "found" it files with a single press-ink-flash in mustard. Bibliography Remove ✕ → HoldToConfirm only if it is permanent (read the code; if it can be re-added from the saved sources, a plain button with an undo is better: say which you chose).
7. EditorialLoader: replace the spinning cobalt ring with a calm set-type line (slugs filling left to right, data-ambient), keeping the rotating wait lines.
8. Editorial Board tabs: the active-tab indicator moves between tabs (a sliding underline using --dur-settle and --ease-set) instead of jumping; unread badges pop once on increment with press-impress (not on every render). Use the paper ink for badge text, not white.

## Rules

## Known issues to fix while you are there (from an inventory)
- Range buttons (7/30/90/All, src/routes/desk/index.tsx ~515-536): the active button adds Tailwind `bg-[var(--color-ink)] text-[var(--color-paper)]` on top of `.btn-paper`, but unlayered `.btn-paper` likely wins over Tailwind v4's layered utilities, so the selected range is visible only via aria-pressed. Verify in a browser and fix in press-desk.css (e.g. `.btn-paper[aria-pressed="true"]` scoped to the desk range nav).
- Every range change sets store.loaded=false and flashes "Reading the ledger" again. Keep the previous figures on screen while the new window loads (mark the section aria-busy and dim slightly), and re-set only the figures that change.
- The local-load task (~256-294) has no try/catch: an IndexedDB failure leaves the page on "Reading the ledger" forever. Add an error state in Twyne's voice.
- Section rules are inconsistent (WritingActivity/UsageCost border-b-2, WriterPatterns none, RecentWork border-t-2, footer border-t-2 → double rules). Make them one rhythm.
- The UsageCost tablist lacks arrow-key handling, aria-controls and roving tabindex. Add them.
- "Selected UTC day"/"This month" labels are hand-built uppercase; use .dept-label.
- Heatmap selected/partial cells use inline boxShadow with no transition; the legend uses rounded-[2px] while cells are rounded-[1px].
- The Desk doesn't listen for USAGE_SYNC_STATE_EVENT (emitted by src/components/desk/usage-sync-controller.tsx), so it doesn't refresh after a sync. Subscribe and re-merge.

## What to build (the joy)

Opening the ledger: figures (Desk facts, cost figures, writer-pattern values, recent-work counts) are set like a composing stick: numerals roll into place ONCE on first arrival (a per-digit translateY roll or an odometer using a registered @property integer with counter(), your choice; respect allowsMotion("feedback")), and never again while the page stays open, except when that specific figure changes after a range switch or sync, in which case only that figure re-sets. The loader "Reading the ledger" should be calm: press-fade with a 150ms delay so fast loads never show it.
2. Range: switching keeps old figures, re-sets only changed ones (see above), no loader flash.
3. Heatmap: selecting a day presses its cell (a 1px inset press with --dur-press, using --ease-platen to release) and the Selected-day aside slides in like a ledger page turning (press-slip-in or press-slip-in-from-right, --dur-arrive). Add a hover state to cells (they have none). Keyboard focus already exists (cobalt); keep it.
4. Charts (DailyActivityChart, UsageCost bars, breakdown fills, token fills): bars rise from the baseline once on arrival (transform: scaleY from 0 with transform-origin bottom, staggered ≤ 12ms per bar, capped total ≤ 400ms; fills grow from left with scaleX). Not on every re-render: only on first arrival or when values change.
5. Patterns (WriterPatterns): when a pattern goes from "Needs N more evidence points" to a value, it receives a small *filed* stamp (reuse the look of `.stamp` rotated, or src/components/ui/workflow-stamp.tsx if it fits) with press-impress, once. 6. Hosted charges: money figures use the credit ink (var(--ink-credit) via data-consequence="credit") and carry a <DestinationTag to="credit" /> where the hosted wallet is described; refreshing re-sets only changed numerals.
7. ChartTable <details>: open/close with a rotating ▸ marker and a height reveal (interpolate-size: allow-keywords under @supports, else just fade), --dur-settle.
8. UsageCost tabs: the active tab indicator slides between tabs (--dur-settle, --ease-set) and the panel crossfades (press-fade).

## Rules
- Durations/easing only from the tokens; no transition: all; no infinite loops (nothing on the Desk is ambient except, optionally, nothing).
- Every animated state has a colour or wording cue for still mode. Charts and figures must be fully readable with motion off (they render at final values immediately under still).

Save before/after screenshots under artifacts/qa-recordings/2026-11-05/juice/lane-d/ (the before state is commit 0fd76e12).

import { Extension, type CommandProps } from "@tiptap/core";
import type { Node as ProseMirrorNode } from "@tiptap/pm/model";

declare module "@tiptap/core" {
  interface Commands<ReturnType> {
    twyneIndent: {
      indent: () => ReturnType;
      outdent: () => ReturnType;
    };
  }
}

/** Indent step, in rem. One tab stop. */
export const INDENT_STEP_REM = 2;

/** How far a paragraph may be pushed before it stops being a paragraph. */
export const MAX_INDENT_LEVEL = 8;

/** Block types that can carry an indent. */
const INDENTABLE = ["paragraph", "heading"];

/** Wrappers whose child paragraph belongs to the list, not to the writer. */
const LIST_ITEMS = ["listItem", "taskItem"];

/**
 * Tab indentation for the manuscript.
 *
 * Tab did nothing in the editor: inside a list Tiptap already nested the item,
 * but everywhere else the key fell through to the browser and moved focus out
 * of the document entirely — pressing Tab while writing a paragraph threw the
 * writer out of their own draft.
 *
 * The rule now matches a word processor: Tab indents the current block one
 * stop, Shift+Tab takes it back, and lists and tables keep the behaviour they
 * already had (nest the item, move to the next cell). The indent is stored as
 * an attribute and rendered as a left margin, so it survives a round-trip
 * through HTML and travels into exports and the PDF rather than being a

Lane A of the living press. The manuscript still never moves; everything
here is colour on the page or furniture around it.

- Wet ink: words set by hand stay in a bluer ink until IndexedDB has the
  draft, then dry through a mid-tone. Painted with the Custom Highlight
  API (no decorations, no DOM) and driven by twyne:draft-saved, so ink
  that stays wet means the save has not landed. Pastes, undo, drops and
  collaborators' edits arrive dry. Typing benchmark (4x CPU) p95/p99 are
  at or below the base commit.

  read from the writer's saved AI and Apparatus settings.

  labelled with what is moving. Removes the off-brand #6d5dfc fallback.

  live: inline on this device offline, account storage when signed in,
  or that sign-in is needed.

content.text:
All three merged without conflicts. The fixes, by lane: **Lane C (room):** 1. Shader: the duration isn't capped below 900ms; the context is lost before resources are freed (acceptable); the rAF loop is fine; the shader key is fine. 2. `freshNoteIds`: `noteId` presence — fine. 3. `UnreadBadge`: the `useTask$` runs on the server too; on first render `previous` equals `count`, so no animation. Fine. 4. The `TraceItem` flash only fires on a status transition. Fine. 5. The bibliography `HoldToConfirm` takes a Qwik `$`; `() => dropEntry(entry.id)` inline is fine. 6. Problem: `.room-trace-reading` and `.room-type-line` use `data-ambient`, which is right, and `.room-reading-ambient` breathes on the `data-ambient` gate. OK. 7. Problem: `.ink-stamp--pressing .ink-stamp__tool` — is that the right class? Need to check. 8. Problem: the readingProgress style `"--reading-progress": number` gives `stroke-dasharray: var(--reading-progress, 0) 1` → `0.35 1` with `pathLength=1`. Fine. 9. Problem: `editorial-board-context--active { border-bottom-color: transparent; }` now loads after global, so the sliding indicator replaces the old static underline. But the indicator uses `width: calc(100% / count)` across a grid with 6 columns; OK. 10. Room destination tags in the rubric: `store.aiSettings` could be null → `credit`. Fine. **Lane B (chrome):** 1. `LastSavedLine` lost the 1Hz tick and the "Saved Xs ago" text, now reading "set / filed / on the wire". The old label had age info; dropping it loses information. Combining them would be better: "set 5s ago" / "filed". I'll restore the age. 2. Text for `savedAt != null` + local-only state → "held on this device · local only". For a signed-out user that's every save, and it's long. Maybe fine but long; the status bar is small. I'll check the visual. 3. `key={filed ? ... : current.kind}` re-mounts the span. OK. 4. Invite with `DestinationTag to="public"`: inviting a collaborator isn't public; it shares with a named person. The contract says "synced, or public if it shares beyond the account". Inviting sends to another person — "public" (vermilion, "Visible to anyone with the link") is inaccurate. I'll override the description, e.g. ``. That's better. 5. The `ShareDialog` `HoldToConfirm` for remove collaborator: the label uses `c.userId` — an ugly ID. Use the name if available. 6. `.press-masthead[hidden]` with `transition: display allow-discrete` — `[hidden]` sets `display:none` via the UA stylesheet; with `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` and `@starting-style` it can animate. Tailwind preflight sets `[hidden]:where(:not([hidden=until-found])) { display: none !important }` in Tailwind v4. `!important` would prevent the display transition from working (display stays none immediately), so the exit animation won't play; the entry via `@starting-style` will work. Acceptable: exit is instant, entry eases. Not harmful. 7. The flow rules in `press-chrome.css` override global flow rules: `[data-flow="flow"] .press-masthead { transform: translateY(-lift-2) }` plus the transition overrides the global `opacity 1.2s ease, visibility 0s linear 1.2s`. Their transition replaces it with `opacity var(--dur-settle)…, visibility var(--dur-settle) allow-discrete`. Global sets `visibility: hidden; opacity: 0` in flow for `.editor-workspace-main > header` — is the masthead that header? Global says `.editor-workspace-main > header`; lane B added the `press-masthead` class to the header. Specificity: `[data-flow="flow"] .press-masthead` (0,2,0) vs `[data-flow="flow"] .editor-workspace-main > header` (0,2,1). Global wins on specificity for header properties, so lane B's transition for the header loses — no effect, harmless. For `.editor-desk-controls`: `[data-flow="flow"] .editor-desk-controls` (0,2,0) in both; press loads later, so its transition wins: `opacity var(--dur-settle)` = 320ms instead of the deliberate slow 1.2s fade. The doc says flow "eases out as one sheet"; the original 1.2s slow fade was deliberate ("chrome fades over 1.2s"). Lane B made the desk controls fade in 320ms while the header still fades in 1.2s — inconsistent. Also settling: `[data-flow="settling"] .editor-desk-controls { opacity: .4 }` is new (desk controls previously didn't dim in settling). Speeding up the flow fade contradicts "ambient/flow should be slow". I'll remove lane B's flow overrides and keep the global 1.2s behaviour, which is calm, deliberate, and already designed. Or keep the settling dim of desk-controls for consistency with the header? The global dims header and toolbar in settling; desk-controls not dimming was maybe an oversight. I'll keep the settling dim but drop the transition override so it inherits... there is no transition on desk controls in settling globally. Simplest: remove the flow block from `press-chrome.css` except the settling dim, with transition `opacity 1.2s ease` to match the global. Use tokens? There's no 1.2s token; `--dur-breath` is 9s. The global uses 1.2s literal. I'll keep matching it with a literal; simpler to delete the block. Then: what does "Zen and flow: chrome eases out as one sheet" need? Lane B implemented `.press-masthead[hidden]` plus `@starting-style` for zen. Fine. 8. `.press-folio-row[data-active="true"]::before` — the vermilion tab uses `--ink-public` as its colour. Semantically wrong: `--ink-public` means public. Use `var(--color-vermilion)` directly. Fix. 9. `.press-drawer-toggle[aria-expanded="true"] svg { rotate 90deg }` — rotating a hamburger 90° makes it vertical lines. Weird, but it signals state. Hmm, odd. Better: keep the icon and change colour only, or rotate... I'll leave colour plus `aria-expanded` and remove the rotation? Rotating the hamburger is a recognizable "open" state in some apps. Remove it for the calmer approach; colour plus title is enough. Actually keep it minimal: remove the rotation. 10. `.press-popover` animation on `.folio` dropdowns — `press-slip-in` includes `rotate(-0.4deg)` from `translateY`; fine. 11. The `folio-menu` modal focus task: `cleanup` focuses `menuTrigger` whenever the dialog value changes, including on unmount. Fine. 12. The `publishedNow` "Published" duplicate button: when `shareUrl` exists and `publishedNow`, it shows a disabled "Published" button with the `press-published` ceremony plus "Live at". OK. 13. `HoldToConfirm` with `disabled={shareBusy.value}` and the label lost its "…" busy state. Minor. 14. Unpublish is permanent? It can re-publish, so it's not irreversible: the reader link is lost but the writer can publish again (a new slug? maybe the same slug). The contract said unpublish → hold. Lane B chose erase. OK. **Lane D (desk):** 1. The `DeskFigure` `useVisibleTask$` sets `animate` true after first paint → digits render static first, then the class is added → the animation plays after visible task → a flash of final values, then roll from below. Since `key={text}` and the animate class is added after mount, the animation starts when the class is applied — digits jump from visible to translateY(100%) and roll in. That's a visible glitch: figure shown, then disappears, then rolls in. Hmm. Since the desk loads data in a visible task too (`store.loaded = false` initially → loader shows → figures mount after data loads), `animate` gets set by the DeskFigure's own visible task... Each `DeskFigure` mounts when the data arrives (after load), and its visible task runs right after mount (document-ready / intersection). The first paint shows digits static, then the class is added on the next tick. Possible flash. Better: decide animation via CSS only: always have `desk-figure-animate` but gate in CSS with `:root[data-motion="still"]` (already handled globally by the still rule: animations collapse to 0.001ms). So simply always apply the animation class — the still rule handles reduced motion. And the "roll once, never again unless changed" requirement: `key={text}` means a re-mount only when the text changes. But also the initial SSR... Desk content renders only client side after load (`store.loaded` false on SSR), so animation on first mount is right. Fix: remove the visible task; always animate. But wait — the "re-set only changed figures" on range switch: DeskFigure gets `key={text}` → only changed figures re-mount → only those roll. Good. Concern: digit roll uses `overflow: hidden` on `.desk-digit` with `inline-block` + `vertical-align: bottom` — this can clip descenders or change line height slightly. Check visually. 2. `.desk-bar` animation: `key` includes values → re-mount on change → re-rise. Good. But for 365 bars ("All" range) with a 2ms stagger capped at 80ms, fine. Problem: the `desk-bar` animation scales the bar container with `scaleY(0)` from bottom. Fine. 3. `.desk-fill` class — is it used in usage-breakdowns/token-dimensions? Check. 4. Heatmap `.desk-heat-cell[aria-pressed="true"] { transform: translateY(1px) }` — the selected cell stays pressed down 1px. OK. 5. `.desk-day` — used on the selected-day aside? Need key on day change to replay. Check writing-activity. 6. Writer patterns: `newlyFiled` computed in a visible task, plus localStorage writes "seen" immediately → the stamp shows once. But the patterns visible task runs on every patterns change; the first time a user opens Desk with available patterns, all available ones get stamped "Filed" (e.g. "Current streak: 1 day" → Filed stamp). On first visit after this ships, every existing user sees all their patterns stamped once. Acceptable: "these patterns are on file". But: `DeskFigure value={value}` where `value` is a string like "Needs 4 more evidence points" → digits roll in "Needs 4 more…". Fine-ish. Problem: the pattern keys are mapped by index to `rows` — fragile but OK if the rows order matches. Check rows order: Current streak, Longest streak, Most active weekday, Most used tool, Most revised folio. And `patternKeys` matches that order: currentStreak, longestStreak, mostActiveWeekday, mostUsedTool, mostRevisedFolio. Need to verify the actual keys of `props.patterns`. Check. 7. The `desk.tsx` loader: `!store.loaded` → loader; on range change, `store.loading` true and `loaded` stays true → content dims (aria-busy). Problem: the error retry button increments `syncRevision`. Fine. Problem: the `store.error` with `store.loaded` true shows a `

` unstyled. Fine. 8. The `.desk-range .btn-paper[aria-pressed="true"]` fix: specificity (0,3,0) beats `.btn-paper:hover` (0,2,0). Good. 9. The usage-cost tabs now keep all panels mounted (hidden) → `desk-panel` fade animation plays when un-hidden? A CSS animation restarts when `display` goes from none to block. Yes — animations restart when an element goes from `display: none` to displayed. Good. But all four panels render their content, including `HostedCost` — fine. The tab indicator: `.desk-tabs::before` with `width: 25%` and `translateX(calc(var(--desk-tab) * 100%))` — grid cols-4 with border-r on each; fine. `desk-tab-active` text colour paper over the ink slider — but the slider is `z-index:-1` within `isolation: isolate`; the tab buttons have no background? Originally inactive tabs had no bg. Fine. So lots of small fixes. I'll do them now in the merged branch. First, verify a few facts: the `stamp-press` class names, the writer-patterns keys, `.desk-fill` usage, `.desk-day` usage.

 * "held here" when they only live on this device. Nothing before the
 * first save, so the line never claims a route for words that do not exist.
 */
export function saveRouteLabel(
  status: SyncStatus,
  savedAt: number | null,
): { word: string; consequence: Extract<Consequence, "local" | "synced"> } | null {
  if (savedAt == null) return null;
  switch (status.kind) {
    case "synced":
      return status.lastSyncedAt >= savedAt
        ? { word: "filed", consequence: "synced" }
        : { word: "on the wire", consequence: "synced" };
    case "pending":
    case "syncing":
      return { word: "on the wire", consequence: "synced" };
    case "offline":
    case "error":
    case "local-only":
      return { word: "held here", consequence: "local" };
  }
}
'''

The lane's impression was a flat halftone disc that hid the grade. The ink
now behaves like ink pressed out from under a stamp:

input.content:
Typing: wet ink that dries when it's saved

The same sentence, typed and then saved. Before, nothing changes. After, new words stay in a bluer ink until IndexedDB has the draft, then dry to black. If the ink stays wet, the save hasn't landed.

Why: the caret and the text are the most frequent thing in the app, so the budget is colour only. Nothing moves or reflows. The ink is painted with the Custom Highlight API, which adds no DOM nodes. The caret is vermilion and never glides (Word's smooth caret makes typing feel late), and the selection is a copy editor's non-photo blue.

Where the words are

The status bar used to show a grey dot. It now says where the latest words are, in that destination's ink: "held here" (hollow, this device), "on the wire", then "filed" in the account's green.

Selecting: every ask says where the passage goes

The toolbar now slides up off the line once per new passage. Find sources and Ask an editor carry a docket dot in their destination's ink, read from your saved settings: mustard when a hosted model reads it and spends credit, cobalt when it's your own model. Comment stays on the device.

Moving the mouse: the desk lamp

A pool of warm light on the desk around the page. It sits where the hour puts it (from the left in the morning, from the right in the evening, warmer at the ends of the day) and leans toward the hand while you aren't typing. It never lights the page itself, so the text's contrast never changes. Broadsheet keeps it off; it rests while you type and below the Full level.

Scrolling: a running foot, and paper sliding under the lamp

The status bar names the section you're reading, like a chapter title at the foot of a book page. The name is set again as you scroll into the next section, and pressing it takes you back to that heading. The lamp stays fixed to the desk, so the paper slides under it.

Dragging: set type, and a docket that says where an image will live

A section's handle is now a type slug. The drop target is a vermilion composing rule that names what's moving. A file dragged in shows a docket saying where the image would be stored: inline on this device when offline, in your account's storage when signed in, or that you need to sign in.

Losing something for good: hold to confirm

Erasing a comment used to be a single unguarded click. Now a quick click erases nothing and shows a "hold to erase" slip; holding the key fills it with ink and erases at the end. Keyboard users press Enter twice. The same guard covers striking the room, removing a source, Stop sharing, removing a collaborator and both Unpublish actions.

Found and fixed while verifying: the first version erased a comment about a second after a plain click. Qwik's handler for the press ran after the release, so the hold never got cancelled. The press is now tracked with native listeners, and a browser test confirms a quick click erases nothing.

The verdict: ink squeezed out from under the stamp

When a new grade lands, a halftone of the grade's own ink is pushed out past the stamp's rays at the moment the wooden die hits. A vermilion second plate sits slightly out of register. It dries away within 0.9s and the WebGL context is then released. It never plays on a restored grade or at the Still level. The shader existed but was imported nowhere before.

The writers' room

The room's three asks share one line saying where the draft goes. The tab underline slides, and Clear became a hold. An editor's portrait shows a reading ring that follows the real stream instead of a spinning ✦.

The reading ring, note arrivals and the per-editor ink impression need a streaming model to see live. They were checked through their components and CSS, not end to end.

Chrome

The File menu now carries a single "device" docket on Export, since exports are files written to this device and nothing is sent anywhere. The active folio in the drawer wears a vermilion tab, and the drawer toggle turns vermilion while it's open.

My Desk

Figures roll into place once when the page opens, and bars rise once. Picking a day presses its cell. Patterns that pass their evidence threshold get a filed stamp the first time. Two bugs fixed: the selected range was invisible, and switching range flashed the loader.

The rules behind all of it

RuleWhat it means in practice
The manuscript never movesNothing animates prose position or layout. Ink may change colour; everything else moves around the page.
Frequency sets the budgetKeystrokes: colour only. Presses: ≤ 120 ms. Arrivals: ≤ 320 ms. Ceremonies such as a verdict or a publish: up to 900 ms.
One ink per destinationdevice · account · your model · hosted credit · public · erased. Always with a word, never colour alone.
Ambient life restsThe lamp, the masthead wobble and the room's listening mark pause while you type, during flow, and below Full.
Still is stillA Motion setting (System / Full / Calm / Still) is applied before first paint. Still stops all movement; state still shows through colour and words.

The full vocabulary sheet (inks, hold states, ring, slugs, springs, durations) is at artifacts/qa-recordings/2026-11-05/juice/page/specimen.webp, and the contract is docs/design/living-press.md.

The status bar names the section you're reading, like a chapter title at the foot of a book page. The name is set again as you scroll into the next section, and pressing it takes you back to that heading. The lamp stays fixed to the desk, so the paper slides under it.

Dragging: set type, and a docket that says where an image will live

A section's handle is now a type slug. The drop target is a vermilion composing rule that names what's moving. A file dragged in shows a docket saying where the image would be stored: inline on this device when offline, in your account's storage when signed in, or that you need to sign in.

Losing something for good: hold to confirm

Erasing a comment used to be a single unguarded click. Now a quick click erases nothing and shows a "hold to erase" slip; holding the key fills it with ink and erases at the end. Keyboard users press Enter twice. The same guard covers striking the room, removing a source, Stop sharing, removing a collaborator and both Unpublish actions.

Found and fixed while verifying: the first version erased a comment about a second after a plain click. Qwik's handler for the press ran after the release, so the hold never got cancelled. The press is now tracked with native listeners, and a browser test confirms a quick click erases nothing.

The verdict: ink squeezed out from under the stamp

When a new grade lands, a halftone of the grade's own ink is pushed out past the stamp's rays at the moment the wooden die hits. A vermilion second plate sits slightly out of register. It dries away within 0.9s and the WebGL context is then released. It never plays on a restored grade or at the Still level. The shader existed but was imported nowhere before.

The writers' room

The room's three asks share one line saying where the draft goes. The tab underline slides, and Clear became a hold. An editor's portrait shows a reading ring that follows the real stream instead of a spinning ✦.

The reading ring, note arrivals and the per-editor ink impression need a streaming model to see live. They were checked through their components and CSS, not end to end.

Chrome

The File menu now carries a single "device" docket on Export, since exports are files written to this device and nothing is sent anywhere. The active folio in the drawer wears a vermilion tab, and the drawer toggle turns vermilion while it's open.

My Desk

Figures roll into place once when the page opens, and bars rise once. Picking a day presses its cell. Patterns that pass their evidence threshold get a filed stamp the first time. Two bugs fixed: the selected range was invisible, and switching range flashed the loader.

The rules behind all of it

RuleWhat it means in practice
The manuscript never movesNothing animates prose position or layout. Ink may change colour; everything else moves around the page.
Frequency sets the budgetKeystrokes: colour only. Presses: ≤ 120 ms. Arrivals: ≤ 320 ms. Ceremonies such as a verdict or a publish: up to 900 ms.
One ink per destinationdevice · account · your model · hosted credit · public · erased. Always with a word, never colour alone.
Ambient life restsThe lamp, the masthead wobble and the room's listening mark pause while you type, during flow, and below Full.
Still is stillA Motion setting (System / Full / Calm / Still) is applied before first paint. Still stops all movement; state still shows through colour and words.

The full vocabulary sheet (inks, hold states, ring, slugs, springs, durations) is at artifacts/qa-recordings/2026-11-05/juice/page/specimen.webp, and the contract is docs/design/living-press.md.

fi

== release.yml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
      - "twyne@*"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.6"

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: bun run build

      - name: Package release bundle
        run: |
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-manual}"
          version="${version#twyne@}"
          mkdir -p release
          tar \
            --exclude="./node_modules" \
            --exclude="./release" \
            --exclude="./.git" \
            -czf "release/twyne-${version}.tar.gz" .

      - name: Publish GitHub release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: release/*.tar.gz
          generate_release_notes: true
          draft: false
          prerelease: false

  # Native desktop builds (Electrobun) — one runner per OS, each uploads its
  # app bundle to the same release the `release` job created. This is what the
  # landing page's "Download Twyne for desktop" link points at.
  desktop:
    needs: release
    name: Desktop (${{ matrix.label }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: macos-latest
            label: macOS
            asset: twyne-desktop-macos
          - os: windows-latest
            label: Windows
            asset: twyne-desktop-windows
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            label: Linux
            asset: twyne-desktop-linux
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: "1.3.6"

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build desktop app
        run: bun run desktop.build

      - name: Archive app bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-manual}"
          mkdir -p dist-desktop
          # electrobun emits the platform bundle under ./build (and any
          # installers under ./artifacts). Archive whatever is produced.
          tar -czf "dist-desktop/${{ matrix.asset }}-${version}.tar.gz" \
            $( [ -d build ] && echo build ) \
            $( [ -d artifacts ] && echo artifacts )

      - name: Upload to release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: dist-desktop/*.tar.gz
          generate_release_notes: false
          draft: false
          prerelease: false

# Changelog

## 0.27.0

<sub>2026-11-05</sub>

- Watch new words dry: what you type stays in a wetter blue-black ink until
  it is saved on this device, then dries to black. Ink that stays wet means
  the save has not landed.
- See where an action sends your words before you press it. Each destination
  has one ink, mark and word everywhere: this device, your account, your own
  model, hosted credit, or public.
- Hold to erase: deleting a comment, striking the room, removing a source,
  stopping sharing, removing a collaborator and unpublishing now ask you to
  hold the key, or press Enter twice, so a stray click cannot lose them.
- Choose how much the room moves in Preferences → Appearance → Motion: Full,
  Calm or Still, following your system by default. Your manuscript never
  moves at any level.
- Work under a desk lamp: a pool of light on the desk around the page, set by
  the hour and leaning toward your hand while you are not typing. Scrolling
  slides the paper under it.
- Keep your place in a long manuscript: the status bar names the section you
  are reading, and pressing it returns to that heading. It also says where
  your latest words are: held here, on the wire, or filed in your account.
- Watch an editor read: a pencil ring around their portrait follows the reply
  as it streams, new notes slip onto the board, and a new grade squeezes a
  little ink out from under the stamp.
- Move a section by its type slug onto a composing rule that names it, and

You are deploying release v0.27.0 of Twyne, a Qwik + Convex web app, to production. The writer who owns the project asked for this release to be cut and deployed, and asked that you (Sol) do the deployment. The release is already prepared and verified locally; your job is to ship it, watch it land, and verify production. Do not edit source code.

## State you start from
- Checkout: /home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/feat-living-press (a git worktree; run everything from there). Branch `feat/living-press`, HEAD `712f56e2 Release v0.27.0: wet ink, holds to erase, a desk lamp and motion levels`.
