- `origin/main` is at `b08cb6f2 Release v0.26.1`, an ancestor of HEAD: pushing HEAD to main is a pure fast-forward of 19 commits (do NOT force-push; if the fast-forward is rejected because main moved, stop and report rather than merging or rebasing).
- `bun run build` (client, SSR server, full typecheck, lint) already passed on this exact commit locally (0 errors, 34 pre-existing lint warnings). You do not need to rebuild locally.
- Previous releases are on GitHub: `gh release list` shows v0.26.1 as Latest.

## How this project deploys (read docs/DEPLOYMENT.md once)
- Production web app: Railway project `twyne` (id 5e255d22-3d03-47db-994e-95ef52acf433), environment `production` (id 8e01b018-ce2b-422d-a46f-de3f1abb7f19), service `twyne` (id c630d82a-98c7-47ed-8faf-9d29c64f0cf7). Railway auto-deploys on every push to `main`. Its build runs `scripts/railway-build.sh`, which also deploys the Convex backend (`npx convex@1.46.0 deploy`) when `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` is set on the service. The `railway` CLI is logged in. Public site: https://www.twyne.love. The last production deploy was v0.26.1 (b08cb6f2), status SUCCESS.
- GitHub Release: pushing a `v*` tag triggers `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which builds, uploads `twyne-<tag>.tar.gz`, and builds desktop bundles for macOS, Windows and Linux into the same release (the landing page's desktop download points at these).
- `bun run release:publish` is `git push --follow-tags` (it pushes the current branch's upstream plus tags). Because this worktree's branch is `feat/living-press`, push explicitly instead:
  `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/main` then `git push origin refs/tags/v0.27.0`.
  Run `bun run release:check` immediately before pushing.

## Steps
1. Pre-flight: confirm HEAD is 712f56e2, `git status` is clean apart from untracked artifacts, the tag points at HEAD, `git fetch origin` and confirm origin/main is still b08cb6f2 (an ancestor of HEAD). Note the current production deployment id with `railway deployment list --project 5e255d22-3d03-47db-994e-95ef52acf433 --environment production --service twyne --json` so you can name the rollback target.
2. Push main (fast-forward), then push the tag.
3. Watch the Railway deployment for 712f56e2 until it reaches SUCCESS or fails (`railway deployment list ... --json`, `railway logs --build <id>` / `railway logs <id>` as needed). Expect several minutes: the build deploys Convex then builds the client and server. If it FAILS: read the build/deploy logs, report the exact failing step and log excerpt, and do NOT attempt code fixes. Production keeps serving the previous deployment when a build fails; if instead the new deployment went live and is broken, redeploy the previous successful deployment (railway `redeploy` of the v0.26.1 deployment id) and report that you did.
4. Watch the GitHub release workflow for the v0.27.0 tag (`gh run list --workflow release.yml`, `gh run watch <id> --exit-status` or poll `gh run view`). Report the `release` job and each desktop job's conclusion and confirm `gh release view v0.27.0` lists the assets. Note: the v0.26.0 release run failed once before, so a failure here is possible; report it with the failing step's log tail, but it does not block the web deploy.
5. Verify production once Railway reports SUCCESS:
   - `curl -sI https://www.twyne.love/` returns 200, and the HTML of https://www.twyne.love/ is served by the new build. Check this concretely, e.g. fetch the page and find the hashed client assets it references, then confirm one of the CSS assets contains strings that exist only in this release: `--ease-slip`, `destination-tag`, `twyne-ink-wet`, `press-running-foot`, `hold-to-confirm`. Also confirm `/editor/`, `/desk/`, `/settings/` return 200.
   - A real-browser smoke test, headless Playwright from the worktree (`node_modules/playwright` is installed; on this machine launch Chromium with `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH node script.mjs`): open https://www.twyne.love/settings/ and confirm the "Motion" radio group (System, Full, Calm, Still) renders and `document.documentElement.dataset.motion` is set; open https://www.twyne.love/ and check for page errors in the console. Do not sign in, do not create accounts, do not submit forms, and do not trigger any AI or paid action against production.
   - Take one screenshot of each page you checked and save them under artifacts/qa-recordings/2026-11-05/juice/deploy/ in the worktree.
6. Do not push anything else, do not change Railway variables or Convex env, do not delete deployments, and do not modify the GitHub release beyond what the workflow creates.

## Report back (concise)
- Push results (main old..new, tag), with timestamps.
- Railway deployment id, status, build duration, and whether Convex deployed (from the build log line "==> Deploying Convex backend" vs "building frontend only").

Pushing main triggers the Railway production auto-deploy (project `twyne`, service `twyne`, which also runs the Convex deploy). input.title: Sol · Twyne loading: find causes and hill-climb the metric
input.task:
The writer who owns Twyne (a Qwik 2 + TipTap + Convex local-first writing app) reports a severe problem: "things are not loading and the loading takes forever". Your job: find the causes and hill-climb a load + responsiveness metric with real, measured fixes. You work in your own git worktree, which starts at `ea1e7ddc` (= origin/main = what production runs right now). Create a branch `perf/loading-hill-climb` there and commit each kept improvement separately. Do NOT push to origin/main, do not deploy, do not touch Railway or Convex settings, and do not sign in to or write to production.

## The metric (already built, use it as-is)
Harness: `/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/perf-harness/perf-metric.mjs` (read its header comment first). It drives Firefox (the reporter's browser) against a production build served by the repo's own `server.js`, seeds a 600-paragraph manuscript into the app's IndexedDB, and measures:
landingMs, openMs (first editor open), editableMs, openWarmMs (second open in the same profile: a returning writer with the service worker active), frameP95/frameMax (pointer wandering over the editor), typeP95 (in-page key -> painted frame), deskMs.
score = (landingMs + openMs + openWarmMs + deskMs)/1000 + (frameP95 + typeP95)/16.7. Lower is better. Do not change the score definition. You may add diagnostics or extra reported fields; if you believe the metric misses the reported symptom, say so and add a separate measure rather than redefining the score.

How to run one measurement of a candidate (from your worktree root):
1. First time only: `bun install`.
2. `bun run build` (about 35s here; it also runs the full typecheck and lint, both must pass).
3. Serve the build: `PORT=5197 node server.js` (background it; restart after every build). Ports 5190, 5194, 5195 are taken by other servers; leave them alone.
4. `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_VALIDATE_HOST_REQUIREMENTS=1 env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH node /home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/perf-harness/perf-metric.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:5197 --engine firefox --reps 5 --paragraphs 600 --label "<what changed>" --out /home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/perf-harness/runs/<n>-<slug>.json`
   (`--sw block` isolates the service worker; `--engine chromium` is available for attribution or profiling, but decisions use Firefox.)
The machine is a busy laptop (other projects compile in the background), so runs are noisy: for small deltas interleave baseline and candidate builds (A/B/A/B) and decide on medians. Keep every run's JSON in that runs/ folder.

## What is already known (evidence, not conclusions; verify)
Earlier measurements on the v0.27.0 build (712f56e2), Firefox, older score definition:
- Production HTTP is fast (TTFB about 0.1s), so the server and network are not the main problem.
- openMs about 3.0-3.5s at 600 paragraphs. At 120 paragraphs openWarmMs (2.69s) was no faster than openMs (2.67s), so client-side work dominates, not network.
- With the service worker allowed, the old score was 11.8 (open 3.48s, desk 1.47s). Blocked, it was 10.9 (open 3.05s, desk 1.12s).
- frameP95 about 50ms while the pointer moves at 600 paragraphs. A separate test on production: lamp leaning (motion=full) p95 33ms, max 99ms; motion=calm, where the lamp does not lean, p95 17ms.

Leads, roughly in order of expected payoff:
1. The editor open is gated. `src/routes/editor/index.tsx` renders only the "Press Room / Setting the type…" gate (around line 1110) until a hydration task (around lines 262-361) finishes a chain of sequential IndexedDB reads. Only then does `TwyneEditor` (`src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx`, around line 927) dynamically import @tiptap/core and every extension and mount the editor.
   - Attribute where the open time goes first (performance marks, or Chromium tracing via `--engine chromium` for a profile). Then cut it. Ideas:
     - Run the reads in parallel, and prefetch TipTap while IndexedDB reads.
     - Render the shell immediately.
     - Defer non-critical extensions and plugins to after first paint or idle: living desk, quick review, struggle tracker or in-flow, mark-anchor widgets, section reorder, pagination, flow conductor.
     - Avoid O(document) work at mount.
2. The service worker (`src/routes/service-worker.ts`).
   - `fetchAndStore` awaits `cache.put(request, response.clone())` before returning the response. So every first fetch of a `/build/` chunk or `/assets/` file is held until the whole body has downloaded and been written to Cache Storage. That includes the 16-28 MB wasm files (typst compiler, onnx runtime, harper).
   - When a fetch fails or is aborted, `respondWith` receives a rejected promise. Firefox then logs "A ServiceWorker intercepted the request and encountered an unexpected error" (seen for `/build/q-*.js` chunks and the harper wasm).
   - Fix ideas: return the network response at once and `event.waitUntil` the cache write. Do not store huge wasm in the SW cache, or store it lazily. Fall back to the network instead of rejecting.
   - Keep the offline behaviour, and keep `src/utils/offline-cache-policy.test.ts` green.
3. Missing static files get a redirect plus an SSR 404. Unknown `/assets/*` and `/build/*` paths return 301 to a trailing-slash URL, then a 404 HTML page (`curl -sI https://twyne.love/assets/LWXDb7Ll-harper_wasm_slim_bg.wasm`). After a deploy, open tabs request old chunk hashes and get this, the module load fails, and Qwik logs "Could not load route …, reloading". Production right now answers v0.27.0's chunk names with 301 because main was redeployed at 14:28 UTC. Serve a fast plain 404 for missing `/build/` and `/assets/` files in `server.js` (no redirect, no SSR) and check that Qwik's recovery behaves.
4. Grammar's wasm. In `src/utils/grammar.ts` (around lines 89-98), harper.js is created with `createBinaryModuleFromUrl(wasmUrl, "full")`. In that mode the library derives a `harper_wasm_slim_bg.wasm` URL from the full one, but the build only emits `harper_wasm_bg.wasm` (15.8 MB), so the slim fetch fails as in lead 3.
   - Find out whether grammar works at all in Firefox and when it loads: the dossier check on /dossier/create/ (anti-tabula-rasa), and the editor's grammar panel.
   - Fix it, for example by emitting the slim binary through a `?url` import and passing it explicitly, and by keeping it off the editor's critical path.
5. A first visit reloads itself. A first visit to /editor/ with no folios redirects to /dossier/create/ and logs "Could not load route /dossier/create/, reloading", which is a full page reload for every new writer. It also logs "error loading dynamically imported module" for chunks that exist and serve 200, e.g. `q-CFI_RvnU.js`, the atproto session module. Determine whether these are aborts caused by the harness's navigations or real failures in a normal visit, and fix the real ones.
6. The desk lamp is expensive in Firefox.
   - In `src/components/editor/desk-lamp.ts` and `src/styles/press-editor.css` (section "The desk lamp"), every pointer move retargets the registered properties `--lamp-x`/`--lamp-y`, which transition for 1.4s. That repaints a full-viewport double radial gradient on the main thread every frame.
   - Keep the idea (a pool of light on the desk that follows the hour and leans toward the pointer when not typing) but make it cheap. For example, paint the gradient once on its own fixed layer and move it with `transform` or `opacity` (compositor-friendly), drop the custom-property transitions, or update far less often.
   - The manuscript must never move or change contrast.
7. Developer experience; does not affect the score. Vite watches `artifacts/` and `.devenv/` and force-reloads every open dev page whenever an `.html` file there changes. The dev log shows lines such as "page reload artifacts/qa-recordings/…/deploy/home.html" and ".devenv/profile/share/doc/…html". Add `server.watch.ignored` for those (and similar output folders) in `vite.config.ts`.
8. Commit ea1e7ddc added a background research loop for signed-in writers (`src/utils/background-research.ts`, `research-route.ts`, `research-verify.ts`). The harness is signed out and cannot measure it. Review statically whether it can flood the network or CPU when the editor opens, and report what you find. Change it only if there is a clear, safe fix.

## Rules for the climb
- Establish the baseline on your own build of ea1e7ddc first, with 5 reps (and one `--sw block` run for reference).
- Then attack the biggest attributable cost first. One change per attempt, measured, kept only if:
  - the score improves beyond noise;
  - errors do not get worse;
  - behaviour is preserved.
- Behaviour to preserve: offline shells still work. The living-press features still work: wet ink, the lamp visible at Full, the running foot, holds to confirm, motion levels. See `docs/design/living-press.md`.
- Revert anything that doesn't improve the score.
- For each kept change, run:
  - the tests next to what you touched (`bun test <files>`);
  - `npx eslint <files>`;
  - `bun run build`.
- Do not run the whole test suite.
- Write commit messages in the repository's style: an imperative summary, a body saying what was slow and why, the before/after medians, and the trailer `Co-Authored-By: GPT-6.1 Sol <noreply@openai.com>`.
- Stop when leads 1-6 are addressed or have proved to be non-issues, or when 3 consecutive attempts fail to improve the score by more than 3%, or after about 15 measured attempts.

input.message:
Extra evidence from the parent, gathered read-only while you work. Fold it into your plan; nothing else changes.

1. Production backend is ruled out:
   - Railway runtime logs since the 14:28 deploy contain only the startup line.
   - The last 500 Convex production executions (14:24-14:53 UTC) are all fast. Queries p95 is under 20 ms, and there are no timeouts.
   - The one failing function is `systemOne:ask`, 2 of 15 runs: "Field name Advice — a specific change would clearly improve it has invalid character '—'". A label containing an em dash is being used as an object field name. It's a correctness bug, not a loading one. Mention it in your report; fix it only if it is trivial and the fix is local to the code that builds that object.
   So "loading takes forever" is client-side.

2. A likely mechanism behind lead 6, worth testing first:
   - `src/styles/motion.css` registers `--lamp-x` and `--lamp-y` with `@property … inherits: true`.
   - `desk-lamp.ts` writes them on `.manuscript-scroller` on every pointermove frame, and press-editor.css transitions them for 1.4s.
   - Because they inherit, each change restyles the whole manuscript subtree, every frame, for the length of the transition. That matches frameP95 rising with paragraph count (about 17 ms at Calm, where the lamp does not lean, against 33-50 ms at Full with 400-600 paragraphs).
   - Try `inherits: false` for both properties first: only the scroller's own background reads them. Then consider a dedicated fixed or pseudo-element layer moved with `transform`.
   - Keep `--press-progress` as `inherits: true`. `.hold-to-confirm__ink` reads it from its parent button.

3. The service-worker cache grows without limit. The writer's own Firefox profile holds 101 MB of Cache Storage for twyne.love and 311 MB for a local 127.0.0.1:5198 origin.
   - `OFFLINE_STATIC_CACHE` keeps every `/build/` chunk from every deploy, plus the 16-28 MB wasm files, forever. `activate` only deletes caches under other names.
   - Under lead 2, evict chunks that no longer belong to the current build, or cap the cache, and keep large wasm out of it unless offline actually needs it.

4. Deploy skew is probably the "things don't load" half of the report.
   - Today there were two deploys 13 minutes apart (14:15 and 14:28 UTC).
   - A tab opened before a deploy keeps running old JS. When it lazily loads a QRL chunk it asks for the old hash, gets a 301 and then an HTML 404, and the handler fails. Buttons and panels then silently stop working until a reload.
   - Under lead 3: as well as the fast plain 404 for missing `/build/` and `/assets/` files, add a guarded recovery for chunk-load failures. For example, listen for Qwik's error event or `unhandledrejection` matching a failed dynamic import of `/build/`, and do one `location.reload()` per session, guarded with a sessionStorage flag. Then the stale tab heals instead of breaking.
   - Measure it if you can: build A, open the editor, rebuild as B with a trivial change, restart the server, interact in the same tab, and confirm the tab recovers.

input.message:
Two more notes from the parent. Nothing here changes your scope or the metric.

1. Service worker, for lead 2. In `src/routes/service-worker.ts`'s fetch handler, every same-origin GET to `/assets/*` (that isn't `/build/`) calls `revalidateStaticAsset(request)` unconditionally, before it looks in the cache. So it serves the cached copy and, every time, downloads the file again and rewrites it to Cache Storage in the background, kept alive by `event.waitUntil`.
   - `/assets/` holds Vite's content-hashed outputs (CSS, the wasm binaries) and the large public art: rubric stamp PNGs of 0.7-1.8 MB each, illuminated initials, persona portraits, page borders and instrument art.
   - Hashed files never change, so a returning writer re-downloads all of them on every page load, competing with the chunks the page actually needs.
   - The Write view does not compile Typst (proof is inactive), so the 28 MB compiler is not on that path. The Proof and export views, harper, and the onnx runtime do go through it.
   - What to do: content-hashed assets should be cache-first with no revalidation. Revalidate only the few stable-named files in the static allow-list. Make `fetchAndStore` hand the response back without waiting for the cache write. Don't let a failed fetch reject inside `respondWith`. Cap or evict the cache.
   - Check the effect with openWarmMs: on a warm open, count the requests the SW makes (with `--engine chromium`, Playwright's `request.serviceWorker()` identifies them).

2. Leave `src/components/collaboration/share-dialog.tsx` alone. I've fixed a regression there on a separate branch: since v0.27.0, the background share check focused the Share button on every auth refresh and pulled the caret out of the manuscript for signed-in writers. Your branch can ignore it and the merge will be clean.

content.text:
I can't reproduce a hang in a clean browser, but I found one regression of my own that's already fixed, and three other problems Sol is now fixing.

**What I measured.** The production server and database are healthy: pages respond in about 0.1 s and backend queries in under 20 ms. In a fresh Firefox profile, signed out, with a 600-paragraph manuscript:
- the landing page loads in about 0.9 s
- the editor opens in about 3.5 s
- My Desk opens in about 1.5 s

That's slow but not "forever". So the severe part probably depends on three things my test doesn't have:
- being signed in
- the 101 MB service-worker cache your Firefox holds for twyne.love
- tabs left open across today's two deploys, 13 minutes apart (v0.27.0, then the Apparatus research commit)

**Confirmed problems:**
1. **Typing lost to the Share button (mine, v0.27.0).** When you're signed in with the masthead showing, a background sharing check moved focus to the Share button. It ran when the editor opened and every time you returned to the tab, so your keystrokes went to the button. The fix is on branch `fix/share-focus-steal` (`44e9062d`); the build passes, but it isn't deployed.
2. **Mouse-move stutter (mine, v0.27.0).** The desk lamp makes the browser redo the styles of the whole manuscript on every frame while the pointer moves. At 600 paragraphs that costs about 50 ms per frame, against about 17 ms without the lamp, and it gets worse as the manuscript grows. Sol is fixing it.
3. **Service worker (older, made worse today):**
   - It holds back each new file until it has finished saving it to the cache.
   - It re-downloads every image and stylesheet in the background on every page load.
   - Its cache never shrinks.

   Sol is fixing it.
4. **Tabs breaking after a deploy (older, made worse today).** A tab opened before a deploy asks for files that no longer exist, gets a "not found" page instead, and that part of the app silently stops working until a full reload. This is probably the "things don't load" half of your report. Sol is adding a fast "not found" response and a one-time automatic reload for these tabs.

There's also an unrelated backend bug: the AI-judgement function fails when a label contains an em dash (2 of the last 15 runs).

Sol is working through these against a load-time and responsiveness score in Firefox, on its own branch, `perf/loading-hill-climb`. It won't push or deploy, and I'll report its before/after numbers when it finishes.

**Until then:**
- Reload any Twyne tab that was open before 09:28 your time.
- Set Preferences → Appearance → Motion to Calm, which turns off the lamp's movement.
- Turn on Zen, which hides the masthead so the focus jump can't happen.

Don't clear site data for twyne.love: that also deletes anything that exists only on this device.

Should I deploy the Share-button fix now? That costs one more deploy, so open tabs need one more reload. The alternative is to ship it together with Sol's fixes in a single deploy.
then deploy once finished

Answer missing build files with a plain 404, and heal tabs a deploy left behind

After a deploy the old build's chunks are gone, but a request for one
was answered with a 301 to a trailing-slash URL and then a full server
render of the 404 page. A module import that expected JavaScript got
HTML, after spending a server render on it. Missing /build/ and
/assets/ files now get a plain, uncacheable 404 straight from the static
handler (no redirect, no SSR).

An open tab that hits a missing chunk now checks whether the server has
moved to a new build (its q:manifest-hash differs from the one the page
was rendered with) and, if so, reloads once to pick it up. It reacts to
Qwik's import-error event, failed dynamic imports and Qwik's "failed to
load" report, but only the server's answer decides; aborted requests, a
lost connection or a handler that threw never reload. At most one such
reload per ten minutes per tab, so a broken deploy cannot loop, and the
editor's pagehide flush keeps typing that is in flight.

Checked across a real rebuild in Firefox: a tab from build A, after the
server moved to build B, still worked for everything it had loaded and
for the chunks the service worker had cached. Drafted by Sol; the
build-hash check replaces its probe of the failing chunk's URL, which
Qwik's error messages do not reliably carry.

content.text:
Yes: with several tabs open, each idle editor tab kept burning CPU. Five tabs together held about one CPU core busy doing nothing. Two never-ending decorations caused it: the wobble on the TWYNE wordmark and the pulsing ring on "Create dossier". Once I fixed those, a third cost turned up (the grammar item below). v0.27.1 fixes all three, and Sol is deploying it now; I'll report when it's live.

Measured in Firefox with the same 600-paragraph manuscript open in every tab:

| Editor tabs | CPU now (idle) | CPU in v0.27.1 | Memory now → v0.27.1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 35% of a core | 16% | 1.2 → 1.0 GB |
| 3 | 84% | 30% | 2.0 → 1.75 GB |
| 5 | 80–128% | 35–37% | 2.7 → 2.45 GB |

A single idle tab on its own drops from about 25% to 6%. Typing stays fast with five tabs open.

**What else is in v0.27.1:**
- **Grammar works again.** The grammar desk in production never finished: it sat on "Checking grammar" because it asked the server for a file that doesn't exist. It now lists suggestions within about 4 seconds.
- **No full-page grammar sweep on open.** Fixing grammar exposed a hidden cost: every time the editor opened, it spell-checked the whole manuscript sentence by sentence, in every tab. That would have pushed an idle tab to about 45% CPU. The page as opened is now taken as written, and only sentences you write or rewrite get checked.
- **Mouse movement no longer stutters** on long manuscripts (Sol's fix to the desk lamp).
- **The caret stays in the manuscript** instead of jumping to the Share button when you're signed in.
- **Missing files fail fast.** A request for a missing file now gets a quick plain "not found" instead of a redirect plus a full server-rendered page.
- **Tabs open during an update reload themselves.** When a tab finds the server has a newer version, it reloads once. I tested it across a real rebuild, but the tab never hit a missing file, so the reload itself hasn't been seen running in a browser. The service worker had already cached what the old tab needed, so it kept working without one.
- **The CI test that runs three tabs at once passes again.** It had been failing because the development server reloaded every page mid-test, not because of Twyne's syncing. That doesn't affect you, but the test can catch real problems again.

**Not fixed: two tabs on the same piece overwrite each other's words.** This has been true since before today.
- Each tab keeps its own copy and saves all of it, so whichever tab saves last wins. In my test, tab A's sentence disappeared once tab B saved, and tab B's disappeared again when A saved next.
- Neither tab shows the other's edits, and no warning appears.
- Signed-in sync doesn't help: it treats a push from another tab as your own and doesn't refresh it.
- Until it's fixed, keep each piece open in only one tab.
- The fix is a design decision: either warn when the same piece is open twice, or have the other tab reload the piece when it gets focus. Tell me which you prefer.

Sol's work also left three items unfinished:
- Opening the editor still takes about 3 seconds at 600 paragraphs.
- The service worker still re-downloads images and stylesheets on every load, and its cache never shrinks.
- A backend function fails on labels containing an em dash.

i think a warning and an option to accept the changes as well maybe preview what is going on

Here's the design I'll build:

- **Warning:** a tab shows a quiet line when the same piece is open in another tab.
- **Notice:** when the other tab saves changes, this tab says so, offering **Preview** and **Bring them in**.
- **Preview:** shows which paragraphs the other tab changed and where both tabs changed the same one.
- **Bringing changes in:** merges paragraph by paragraph, so edits in different places both survive.
- **No loss:** if this tab is about to save over the other tab's newer version, that version is kept in Versions first.

Instead, seed like `e2e/instruments.e2e.ts` `seed()`: route `/api/auth/` to `null`, visit a routed blank page, `import("/src/utils/idb.ts")` in page context, then call saveFoliosToIdb / saveFolioContentToIdb / saveActiveFolioIdToIdb (+ `signin-toast-dismissed` meta, `twyne:editor:view:v1` with zenMode false).

It starts its own server on 5187 and compares against the committed `e2e/visual-baselines/`. The default config writes stray `e2e/*-snapshots/` folders; delete them afterwards.

    - Tests expect a visible `.twyne-toolbar`, Bold, or read-aloud control, but zen is now the default and those sit in the collapsed Compositor. This breaks __responsive, select-all and read-aloud.
    - Tests expect a "File ▾" button and other masthead and drawer flows that have since changed. This breaks import and dossier-persistence.

input.title: Hover cards that stay and can be used
input.task:
You are working on Twyne, a local-first writing app (Qwik 2 + TipTap/ProseMirror + Convex). Your goal is to make the editor's hover cards stay and be usable. Here is the request in the user's own words:

> "the users when they see the hover effect they want to be able to interact with the editor that pops up and we should have a effect where the hover card that appears sticks around while the user has seen it for a time so that the user can go click on it send a reply get the non truncated view."

## First steps
- Your worktree starts from an older local commit. Begin with `git fetch origin && git switch -c feat/hover-cards-stay origin/main`. `main` is v0.27.1. Run `bun install` if the lockfile changed.
- Read `CLAUDE.md`.
- Read these notes in `/home/diogenes/.claude/projects/-home-diogenes-Projects-apps-twyne/memory/`:
  - `twyne-browser-verification.md`: the headless Playwright recipe, IndexedDB seeding, and how to open suggestion cards.
  - `skip-long-verification.md`
  - `autonomy-by-default.md`
  - `no-reflexive-hedging.md`
- Run the dev server on **port 5182**: `TWYNE_DEV_PORT=5182 bun run dev.frontend`.

## Where the hover paths are
There are two, and both need the fix.

1. **The floating card when the margin is not carrying notes.** In `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx`, around the comment "Hover: preview a persona note below its sentence" (about line 1980):
   - `mouseover`/`mouseout` on `.twyne-persona-note`, `.twyne-comment-mark` and `.twyne-mark-anchor` drive it;
   - the state lives in `store.notePopover` / `store.userCommentPopover`, with `buildAndPin` and `OPEN_WRITER_COMMENT_EVENT`;
   - there is a 350 ms intent delay;
   - today it closes on mouseout unless `relatedTarget` is already the card. Crossing the gap between the passage and the card closes it.
2. **The margin.** `src/components/in-flow/flow-surface.tsx` uses `hoverId`/`peekId`/`lingerId`/`openId` and `hover()`. Pointing at a passage peeks its card there and draws a connection.

## What to build
A hover card the writer has actually looked at should stay.
- **Dwell.** After the card has been visible for a short dwell (pick it; roughly 600–900 ms), it becomes held. A quick pass-through never holds anything.
- **Crossing the gap.** Add a grace period and treat the pointer heading toward the card (a safe triangle) as staying. Moving from the passage to the card never closes it.
- **While held, the card is fully interactive:**
  - click into it;
  - write and send a reply in its thread;
  - expand it to the untruncated text;
  - use its existing actions.
- **It goes away** on Escape, a click elsewhere, typing in the manuscript, or a deliberate hover on another passage after a grace period.
- **Focus.** It must never steal the caret or focus while the writer is typing. v0.27.1 fixed a focus steal (`src/components/collaboration/share-dialog-focus.test.ts`); don't regress that kind of behaviour.
- **Show the held state.** Use the living-press motion system in `src/styles/motion.css`: tokens like `--dur-settle` and `--ease-set`, and keyframes like `press-impress`. For example, the card settles and pins with a subtle impression. Respect the `html[data-motion]` levels full, calm and still.
- **Zen mode** keeps its current rule: hover previews are suppressed.

## Tests and verification
- Put the hover state machine (intent, dwell, grace, held, dismiss) in a small pure module with unit tests.
- In the browser, use Playwright to:
  - move the mouse from a marked passage to its card across the gap, slowly and with a realistic path;
  - check it stays held;
  - type a reply and send it;
  - expand the full text;
  - check Escape and typing dismiss it, and a quick pass-through does not hold it.
- Check both the floating path (margin hidden) and the margin path.
- Seed a folio with persona notes or comments in IndexedDB. Look at how existing e2e tests seed them (`e2e/`).

Thanks. The sheet is a good base. Please continue on the same branch (`feat/scene-bench-media`) and finish the generation half. You were right that a wallet check alone can't settle a direct fal charge, and here is how that resolves.

**"Our fal key" is the Not Organic gateway's `FAL_KEY`.** The gateway lives at `/home/diogenes/Projects/notorganic-provider`; read it there. Hosted generation goes through the gateway, which reserves and settles credit itself. Twyne needs no `FAL_KEY` of its own in Convex, so don't add a direct fal call to Convex. The relevant gateway pieces:

| Gateway piece | Where | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/images/generations`, alias `image` | already used by `convex/sceneMedia.ts` `sceneMedia:picture` via `hostedRoute(...)` | **Look.** Reuse it for 2–3 variants (literal, imagined, a style), each prompt built from the sheet. |
| `/v1/videos/generations` (POST) and `/v1/videos/generations/:jobId` (GET) | `apps/gateway/src/app.ts:733`, `apps/gateway/src/video.ts` | **Motion.** Models `video` / `video-fast`; image-to-video when `image_url` is given; async job with reserve/settle. Scopes `videos:generate` / `videos:read`. |
| `/v1/fal/jobs` (POST) and `/v1/fal/jobs/:id` (GET) | `apps/gateway/src/fal.ts` | `image-animate` (Seedance image-to-video), `image-edit`, `image-segment`. Scope `infer:image`. |
| Hosted transport and token issuing | `convex/lib/notorganic.ts`: `issueNotOrganicAccessToken`, `notOrganicOpenAiRoute`, `NOTORGANIC_MODEL_ALIASES`, `NOTORGANIC_ALIAS_CEILINGS_MICROUSD` | How Convex calls the gateway. |

What to build:
1. **Hosted look.** Variants through the existing `image` alias, prompts from the sheet.
2. **Hosted motion.** Image-to-video from a look the writer picks, or the first one when it runs by itself, through `/v1/videos/generations` with `video-fast`.
   - Add Convex actions to submit and poll. Issue the token with the right capabilities.
   - Keep it async: submit returns a job id, and the client polls with backoff.
   - Add an alias or ceiling entry in `convex/lib/notorganic.ts` if needed.
   - If the gateway's product policy may refuse Twyne the `videos:*` scopes, say so in your report rather than guessing.
3. **Hosted sound.** The gateway has no route for sound effects or ambience. Add one in `/home/diogenes/Projects/notorganic-provider`:
   - work on a new local branch `feat/scene-sound` there;
   - a new fal alias in `apps/gateway/src/fal.ts` (for example `sound-scene`) with a current fal model;
   - candidates to check in fal's docs: a sound-effects or ambience model, or MMAudio (video-to-audio) to score a motion clip. Use current model IDs from fal's docs, not guesses;
   - follow the existing validate, reserve, settle, poll pattern and its env-driven price;
   - write tests next to the existing ones (`tests/async-media-accounting.test.ts`, `apps/gateway/src/*.test.ts`);
   - commit locally only. Do not push or deploy the gateway.
   
   On the Twyne side, call it the same way as motion. Until that gateway branch ships, the hosted sound button explains that it isn't available yet. The writer's own fal key path (item 4) still works for sound.
4. **The writer's own fal key.** Add it in scene media settings, stored like other bring-your-own provider keys.
   - The client calls `queue.fal.run` directly for look, motion and sound.
   - Check CORS. If browsers can't call fal directly, say so and route through a minimal relay that never stores the key.
5. **Storage and playback.**
   - Media blobs live in IndexedDB, keyed by passage, and stay out of manuscript evidence.
   - Show takes per medium in the bench, with compare and playback.
   - Prompts come from the sheet, including inferred entries clearly marked as interpretation.
6. **Running by itself.** Once generation is on in Settings, opening the bench prepares the sheet and the first look by itself, within budget. Motion and sound start with one click, since they cost more. Never run when generation is off.
7. **Tests and verification.**
   - Unit tests with mocked gateway and fal: submit, poll, settle and failure paths.
   - A mocked browser run of the bench: sheet, takes, playback.
   - Rerun `bun run build` and get it green. The last one failed.
   - Same limits as before: no live paid calls unless `skate get fal-key` returns a key (at most about 6, cheapest models); no Convex or Railway env changes; no push.

Report back:
- Branch heads in both repos.
- Model IDs, with links to fal's docs.
- What changed, as file:line.
- What env or deploy the gateway branch needs to ship, including price env vars.
- Verification results.

The flicker lane is done, and I've reviewed its diff. The fixes target real causes, and none of them work by switching animations off. This is committed as `c82a2cdb` on `fix/flicker-during-model-runs`; nothing is pushed or deployed.

**What was causing it:**
- **The flicker:** every streamed word from a model reset the reply card's "freshness". The margin re-sorted on each token, moving the cards and replaying their entrance animations over and over. Freshness now resets once, when a reply starts.
- **The scroll jumping:** each incoming persona note moved your caret to the passage it quoted. Notes now arrive together in one step, without touching your selection or scroll and without adding an undo step.
- **The repeated warnings:**
  - Live review and quick review told you to connect your account even when you were using your own model, which needs no account. Both now just ask your model.
  - A failed review retry briefly cleared its warning on each retry and re-inserted it when the retry failed. It now stays put until that review actually succeeds. Three failed retries leave one notice instead of a flashing one.
- **Console noise:** three components that render nothing produced startup warnings every time the editor loaded. Those warnings are gone.

**Measured over 10 seconds of scrolling with three model replies streaming:**

| | Firefox | Chromium |
|---|---|---|
| Cards moved through the page | 47 → 0 | 33 → 0 |
| Layout shifts | not measurable in Firefox | 20 → 14 (total shift about 11× smaller) |

Frames over 50 ms were unchanged (2 in Firefox, 1 in Chromium). No console errors showed in either browser before or after. Its 32 targeted tests and the build passed.

**Not verified:** actual inference with an on-device (WebGPU) model, because the test browser had no model weights. A live review that succeeds also wasn't run; its local test endpoint was deliberately failing. If your flicker happened with an on-device model running, that path still needs a real test.

The hover-card, line-editor and Scene Bench lanes are still running. Once they're in, I'll put all five branches together for one release, but only if you want it deployed.

content.text:
The hover-card lane is finished and I've reviewed its diff. It's committed as `bc1a95b0` on `feat/hover-cards-stay`, not pushed or deployed.

**How it behaves now:**
- **Opening:** after you hover a marked passage for 350 ms, its card opens.
- **Staying:** once it has been open for 750 ms, it stays, with a slight settling motion. That respects the full, calm and still motion levels.
- **Getting to it:** heading from the passage toward the card counts as staying, with 450 ms of grace. Crossing the gap no longer closes it.
- **While it stays:** you can click into it, write and send a reply, and expand it to the full untruncated note, without the caret leaving your manuscript.
- **Passing over another note** while one is held doesn't replace it. You have to hover the new one deliberately.
- **Closing:** Escape, clicking elsewhere, or typing in the manuscript, and your caret stays where it was. A quick pass-over never makes a card stay.
- **Both kinds of card** behave this way: the floating card and the margin card.

The reopen-after-Escape bug from the first round had two causes, one in the code and one in its test:
- The code kept a stale "pointer is over the card" flag after Escape, which cancelled the next hover.
- The browser test hovered at old coordinates after the page had shifted, so it missed the passage.

Both are fixed, with a unit test for Escape then reopen.

**Checks:** the browser test passed on both kinds of card, covering every behaviour above. The four unit tests and the build passed. The two lint warnings it reports were already on main.

The timing logic sits in its own module. It's written more densely than the rest of the codebase, so I'll run the formatter over it when I combine the branches.

Scene Bench can now make a scene's look, sound and motion, and I confirmed it with real fal calls using your key. I've sent the lane back for three remaining pieces; it's committed as `7cb5e944` on `feat/scene-bench-media`, not pushed.

The lane's own live run broke off partway, so I ran a scene through Twyne's own fal code: "a salt road at dusk, a mule cart with lanterns, wind off the sea, gulls, wheels creaking on wet stones".

| Medium | Model | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Look | FLUX.1 Schnell | 4 s | 1024×768 image |
| Sound | CassetteAI sound effects | 67 s | 5 s stereo WAV; plays in Firefox and Chromium as stored |
| Motion | MiniMax Hailuo 02, from the look | 83 s | 6 s clip |

![look](/tmp/scene-live/look-small.jpg)
![motion, first and last frame](/tmp/scene-live/motion-strip.jpg)

The full clip is `/tmp/scene-live/motion.mp4`, and the sound is `/tmp/scene-live/sound.bin` (a WAV).

fal didn't return a cost for any call; your fal dashboard has it. The lane's interrupted run may also have charged for one sound. The motion clip is by far the most expensive of the three.

**How it works in the bench:**
- **Scene sheet:** Clairic reads the passage into setting, light, characters, motion, sound and mood, each tied to the words it came from. Generation prompts are built from that sheet.
- **Automatic first look:** once generation is on in Settings, opening the bench on a scene makes a first look by itself. More looks, sound and motion are one click each.
- **Playback:** takes are kept on the device per passage, played back in the bench, and stay out of the manuscript.
- **Two ways to pay:** your own fal key, kept on the device, or Twyne credit through the Not Organic gateway, which charges the writer itself. Twyne needs no fal key in Convex.

**Gateway branch:** `feat/scene-sound` at `4065d2c3`, in its own worktree. It adds the hosted sound route; its 45 media and accounting tests pass. It also makes the gateway's job store accept fal jobs, which it didn't before. To ship hosted sound and motion you'd need to:
- deploy the gateway branch;
- set `FAL_SOUND_SCENE_PRICE_MICROUSD`, plus `VIDEO_FAST_PRICE_PER_SECOND_MICROUSD` for motion. CassetteAI's listed price is $0.01 per generation; the price you set is what writers pay;
- confirm the live gateway lets Twyne use the video permissions. That's only been checked locally.

**Conflict in your main gateway checkout:** `/home/diogenes/Projects/notorganic-provider` has uncommitted work that isn't from this lane (speech dispatch, named models). It edits the same line of `convex/asyncMedia.ts` as the sound branch, so merging them will need a one-line fix.

**Sent back to the lane** (no new live calls):
- **Takes survive a reload.** Today a reload or closed bench during an 80-second motion take loses a take you've already paid for. Pending jobs will be saved and resumed; the key itself is never stored.
- **One automatic-generation limit across tabs.** Right now each tab has its own limit, so two tabs double the automatic spend.
- **Filling the gaps.** Where the passage leaves something open, like light, palette or sound, the sheet will suggest an interpretation, clearly marked as one.

**Status of everything:**

| Work | State |
|---|---|
| Two-tab warning, flicker fix, hover cards | Done |
| Scene Bench | Finishing the three items above |
| Line editor (Fable) | Still running |

When those two land, I'll combine everything into one release, but only deploy if you say so.

content.text:
I picked up the line editor from where Fable stopped. It's finished and merged into `release/0.28`, which builds and passes its tests. Nothing is pushed or deployed.

**How Line edits works:**
- **What it reads.** It only looks at sentences you write or rewrite in this session, once they settle. The document you opened is taken as written.
- **What it flags.** Harper's grammar findings plus cheap local checks (a repeated word, a dangling opener, chained clauses, stacked hedges, a double negative) pick the sentences worth asking about.
- **Asking the model.** Only flagged sentences go to your model, one at a time when the tab is idle, once per wording, with a cap per session. Signed-in writers without their own model get rewrites from three editors in the writers' room instead.
- **In the editor.** A flagged sentence with rewrites ready gets a faint dotted underline. Resting the caret there opens a margin card with the reason, the model's note, and 3–5 labelled rewrites shown as word-by-word changes.
- **The buttons.** "Use" swaps the rewrite in as one undo step. "Work on it" opens it in Compare a revision. "Leave it" is remembered, so that sentence isn't raised again, even after a reload.
- **Safety.** A rewrite that drops any of your numbers is refused.

![Line edits card](/home/diogenes/.t3/worktrees/twyne/t3-1b8bf5f1/public/assets/instruments/line-edits-card-v1.png)

**What I fixed on top of Fable's work:**
- **The "Use" buttons couldn't be clicked.** The margin's empty column was covering the card and swallowing clicks. I changed the margin CSS so empty margin no longer blocks clicks, which affects every margin card, not just this one. The existing margin browser tests still pass.
- **The build failed** on two type errors in Fable's test file. Fixed.
- **The browser test typed into the middle of another sentence**, because End only goes to the end of the visual line. Fixed.
- **The manual's new Line edits chapter** pointed at two screenshots that didn't exist. I saved the test's captures as those images.

**Checks:**
- The browser test passes end to end: flagged, underlined, card opens, Use, undo, cached with no second model call, and Leave it remembered after a reload.
- Idle-tab CPU, with your own model connected and live review on: 9–10% on the release branch without Line edits, 9% with it. No model requests while idle.
- Three tests in an older browser suite (`instruments.e2e.ts`) fail, two for missing screenshot baselines and one on a stray empty style attribute. Their sentence and margin steps passed; they weren't run on main, so I haven't confirmed whether main fails the same way.

**`release/0.28` is now at `49f581da`**, with all five features: the two-tab warning, the flicker fix, hover cards, Scene Bench, and Line edits. The 129 targeted tests and the build pass.

Shall I cut v0.28.0 and have Sol deploy it? Without the gateway's `feat/scene-sound` branch, hosted Scene Bench generation covers looks only; sound and motion work with a writer's own fal key.
